**'l. f** uch attention has been given co the activities of Mutants and cultists **_lY_ land** those who hunt them, but the Empire is a far-larger place than a few beleaguered communities. Between these outposts of civilisation, there 

are large swathes of wilderness holding terrible secrets mankind was not meant co know and vicious creatures that defy imagination. By examining these wild places, one can learn something of Chaos in its purest form. 

###### **l.mJNTHI Wui>BUIB** 

T here are two worlds in the Empire. with streets, patrols of soldiers, popuOne lated by is the common world of man and the city, noble, entertainer and beggars. These are the centres of industry, the great hope of the future. Commoners drift towards the cities for the work and wealth they promise, leaving behind the life of a rustic. But cities are not all glamour and prosperity. They are havens for criminals, hotbeds for disease, and power can be won and lost in a single day. They also produce Mutants, shelter cults, and are home co grifters, criminals, and thieves. 

The other world is free from the petty corruption and underhanded ways of urban life. It _is_ the countryside. It is a world of hard work, but also of great reward. Close-knit communities provide comfort and security, engendering a sense of belonging, unlike the alienation and isolation of the big metropolises. While these isolated villages are removed from the huscle and bustle of city life, they face many of the same dangers and many other ones as well. Not free from the occasional Mutant, the perverse Witch, and the insidious machinations of the Chaos cults, they also must contend with "what's out there." 

The Empire's wilderness is largely unexplored. Whilst maps exist, there has yet to be a successful effort co record every scream, every hill, and every cown, and even more importantly, nearly all maps contradict each other. Speckled throughout the countryside are castles, fores, coaching inns along the various roads, and villages. Beyond these isolated pockets of civilisation are vast stretches of forest and plains, criss-crossed by game trails and old footpaths. It is here, in the great unknown, that the monsters live. 

Roaming the wilds are herds ofBeastmen, foul creatures blending the characteristics of man and beast, and their cousin races of Dragon Ogres, Minotaurs, and worse. In addition, tribes of Goblins and pockets of res squat in the shadows of the dim forests, while darker things lurk squat in the shadows of the dim forests, while darker things lurk of the dim forests, while darker things lurk the dim forests, while darker things lurk dim forests, while darker things lurk forests, while darker things lurk

The threat of attack looms over those who eschew the protection of a city's walls, so O ld Worlders, and the Empire, have taken seeps to protect the countryside. And the few scattered settlements offer some protection by dint of their numbers, co say nothing of their militia. 

###### **CoACHING HOUSES** 

Travel in the Empire is difficult and perilous. The roads are uncertainunsafe in the best of times, impassable in the worst. To ameliorate the worst of the difficulties, a number of powerful coaching services erected coaching houses along the various routes through the Empire. The most famous of these is the Four Seasons, which has expanded beyond its base in Altdorf and along all the routes out of the capital. Other Coaching Lines include Carcak Lines and Ratchett Lines, both centred in Altdorf; Red Arrow Coaches of Averheim: Wolf Runner Coaches and Castle Rock

###### **Hollow Grey**

Inside each are tables with old trenchers and tankards arranged as if the people disappeared in the midst of a meal. ###### **EL VEN WA YSTONES**

The Wayscones became foci of incredible magical energy, supporting and reinforcing the Vortex ofUlchuan that siphoned magic from the world. 

###### **<u>s</u> Using Waystone** 

Since Waystones and similar formations are nexuses of magic, it stands co reason that Wizards and their ilk are attracted co these locations since they can tap the magical currencs more easily on Leylines and near Wayscones than they can elsewhere. More so than the sanctioned Wizards, these places are doubly attractive to chose who practice Dark Magic, since it heightens their ability to control _Dhar_ and manage the various Winds they exploit. During the Scorm of Chaos, Archaon's Thrall Wizards and cultists seized these locations wherever they could co enhance their strength against the Colleges of Magic and chei **r** allies. When casting spells in proximity co a Wayscone, spellcasters gain a + ld5 bonus to each d 10 used in the Casting Roll.

The _Old World Bestiary_ provides a great deal of information on Beascmen and how they are perceived and understood in the Old World, as well as providing statistics for average examples of the various breeds and types. However, Beascmen are a diverse species with all sores of subtle differences between chem. With the following rules, it's possible for you co create Beascman characters for use as Player Characters. Unless you enjoy eating babies, butchering Humans, and roaming from place co place until you are finally overwhelmed by Imperial soldiers, these characters are probably not suitable for the average game. But groups featuring Chaos Warriors and Mutants might cake on Beascmen as part of their encourage. There is something darkly appealing co playing agents of Chaos, and so the following is designed co accommodate all kinds of games, whether for creating unique adversaries or for creating bold Champions of Chaos. 

- _Silent as the Beasts of the Woods:_ Beascmen are naturally stealthy. They gain a +20% bonus co Silent Move Tescs and a +10% co Concealment Tests. 

###### **GAINING MORE MUTATIONS** 

Beascmen gain more mutations in the same ways chat Humans do. However, since all Beascmen begin play with at lease two mutations, they are at greater risk of gaining additional ones. A Beascman can have a maximum number of mutations equal co **ldlO** + **1** + **its Toughness Bonus.** 

###### **GORS**

As well, Beascmen may advance into the Chaos Warrior Career described in **Chapter XIII: Slaves to Darkness.**

###### **<u>s</u> Bovigor** 

Bovigors are those Gors who have cattle horns on their head and may have the entire head of a bull or ox. Bovigors are highly competitive and see themselves as superior co all other Gors. Most have little use for thinking, preferring instead co use their mighty strength co solve problems. 

###### **~~s~~ u.ptigor** 

More common than all other types of Gors, Caprigors have curling or straight horns on their head, like a goat or ram. Most Caprigors may have the entire head of a goat, and if so, they also have matching goat legs. 

###### **<u>s</u> Truegor** 

A Beastman that has fine horns and no other mutations is called a Truegor. Truegors have either Human or goat legs. These rare Beastmen are the most intelligent and strongest of all of their kind, almost always rising to positions of great honour within the herd. 

###### **~~Additional Racial Features~~** 

Gors have the following additional skills and talenrs. 

**Skills:** Intimidate 

**Talents:** Menacing, Savvy (Truegor only), Very Strong (Bovigor and Truegor only) 

**Additional Mutations:** All Gors begin play with Animalistic Legs, Bestial Appearance, and Horns. Bovigors also gain H ulking Brute. 

**Trappings:** Light Armour (Leather Jack), a Hand Weapon _or_ Spear, and a Hand Weapon _or_ Shield. 

###### **<u>s</u> Bestigor** 

The toughest of Beastmen are known as Bestigors. As well as being stronger, they tend to be more disciplined, forming more organised ranks in battle than their quarrelsome lesser brethren, and they restrain themselves from their more disruptive excesses. They always wield the best weapons and wear the best armour available to the herd, sometimes even using weaponry culled from the corpses of their enemies. 

Bestigor is presented here as a career. Most Bestigors have five or six advances. Only the rarest and most powerful have more.

###### **GAVES** 

Throughout the lands of the Empire and northwards, it is not uncommon for healthy Human parents co produce a Mutant child. Some try co conceal their baby's deformities, but most feel such shame chat they give chem up co the forests and rivers, abandoning chem co die from hunger or exposure. The Beascmen are keen for the whimpers of these lose children. Such foundlings are always adopted and reared with the rest of the herd, since the Beascmen regard these infancs as gifcs from their Gods. 

These Mutants are called Gaves or Gave Children. _As_ they grow, they often become Gors, Ungors, or even Brays, but the rest of the herd do not apply the same stigma chat they do ochers of their kind since they are holy (or, rather, unholy) gifts, and any Gave can rise high in Beascman society. 

###### **BRA Y--SHAMANS** 

All users of magic muse tap inco the magical energies loosed from the Realm of Chaos, but Bray-Shamans use chis energy in a natural, almost instinctual way. They are born knowing how co wield Chaos energy in ics raw form like ocher Beascmen seem co know how co hunt, track, and kill. Therefore, Bray-Shamans need not study or undergo special training; they simply know. 

One of the most important powers employed by these Beascmen is their ability co send their consciousness inco the Realm of Chaos, there co converse with the Daemons and even the Gods they find there. They reach chis plane by drinking themselves inco a stupor and breaching the fumes of hallucinogenic planes thrown inco the fires at the base of the Herdscone. Their ability co commune with the Gods ensures they are safe from attacks by the rest of the Warherd, since all Beascmen believe chat harming a Bray-Shaman means utter annihilation at the hands of their foul Gods. 

Bray-Shamans are physically similar co Gors. What separates chem from ochers of their kind is the colour of their eyes. The colours signify which Chaos Power favours the Shaman: blue or yellow for Tzeencch, green or brown for Nurgle, pink or purple for Slaanesh, and bright red for Khorne (though Shamans of Khorne never case spells). They typically dress in elaborate gowns or decorated hoods. Mose carry staves (specifically Brayscaves, see sidebar for details) and often banners decorated with scalps and bones. 

Bray-Shamans gain Rewards and Gifcs of Chaos just as Chaos Warriors and Chaos Sorcerers do.

###### **Doombulls**

###### **THE CHAMPION'S FEAST** 

Should the Beascman leader fall, the entire herd comes together co mourn his passage in a raucous feast with dancing and debauchery. If the fallen Champion was particularly famous, ocher Warherds may attend in his 

honour. The Champion's body is eaten by the most loyal followers, leaving che most tender and choicest bics for the eldest and the most-favoured advisors. If che new Champion was the old one's follower, he cakes the heart co devour in one gulp, all co the roars of approval from the gathered hose. The Beascmen believe a warrior's essence is in his heart, and by devouring the heart of an old Champion, the wisdom and power passes on co his successor. 

The Champion's Feast is a great tradition among the herds, so they are careful co recover che body of fallen leaders. Should the body be utterly destroyed, or otherwise unrecoverable, it is viewed as a bad omen worthy enough co consult the Warherd's Bray-Shaman for guidance. 

###### **HERDSTONES** 

Herdscones are integral to Beascman beliefs, serving as mustering points for Warherds. The scones are usually rock outcroppings or old monoliths. Often hidden in a cave or a remote vale, the secrecy of a Herdscone is integral co the spiritual beliefs of the Beascmen. Many Herdscones uncovered in che wilderness are surrounded by bones, charred wood, and dung. The smoke-stained rock normally has the symbol or rune of the Beastman who put it there. 

###### **THE BRA** YHERD 

Under normal circumstances, rival Warherds have little loyalty co one another, battling each ocher as much as they do Humans and ocher races. Confliccs spark over territory disputes, loot, or no reason at all. From time co time, the Warherds unite co oppose a common threat or when the powers of Chaos join for one of the dreaded Incursions and gather at a Herdscone co consult the wisdom of the Bray-Shamans. Such meetings are called Brayherds. 

Any Champion can call for a Brayherd by lighting a bonfire at the base of a Herdscone. He piles on green wood, Brays, and captives, using the scent of charring meat co attract the roaming Warherds. Once assembled, the Champion lays out the purpose of the Brayherd. As almost all such gatherings are assembled co plan an attack, the Champion muse convince the ocher herds of his plan and reasons. The ocher Champions weigh his words and must decide whether they will join his cause. While the Champions converse, the rest of the Beascmen enjoy a raucous celebration of feasting, fighting, and drinking. Bray-Shamans regale the herds with tales of famous battles and even cs significant co the Beascmen race. 

Once all agree co cake part in the attack, there is a grand battle between the Champions called a Gorfighc. Each Champion has his hands tied behind his back and muse defeat all of his rivals using only his horns. Hence, only Gors usually participate. When Ungors participate, the ochers gang up co crush him first. The contest cakes place in a ring around the Herdscone, and all the ocher Beascmen press in co watch. Spectators can strike out with fists and clubs at anyone who comes coo close co the edge-many Gors have been swallowed by the press of mutated flesh, trampled and beaten co death by an overenthusiastic audience. In the end, there is only one winner-the lase one standing.

###### **A SAMPLE w ARHERD** 

Deep in the Drakwald forest, something violent and uncontrollable has stirred. After a number ofBeastmen have vanished, chewed inro bloody gobbets of _Resh_ and bone by a Chaos Spawn's drooling jaws, the Beastmen decide tO move to a new camp. Calling a Brayherd, they call other herds ofBeastmen tO create a potent force tO protect the herd as it moves tO a new location. The Bray-Shaman piles wood and rotting meat on the fires built around the Herdstone, and, in small clumps, many Beastmen come forth to meet with the other leaders. Once a good number are assembled, the Bestigors and Champions scratch their names in the Herdsrone and settle near the fire to listen to the Bray-Shaman relate what is going on in their territory. 

Whilst the advisor speaks, a great crowd of Gors, Brays, and Ungors congregates ourside the ring ofleaders, fighting, braying, and tormenting each other as they jockey for places closer to the fires. The Gors gain the warmest places, where the best food is kept, while the Ungors and Brays fight for space just beyond the edge of light, fighting for whatever scraps are thrown tO them by their betters. Warhounds snarl and fight amongst each other in their pens while the Tuskgors root around in the offal for food not even the Brays would touch. 

as Over the next few days, Beastmen leave for various reasons such pride, hunger, or even curiosity; in the end, there are still a goodly number of Beastmen left. The Bray-Shaman throws a handful of dust inro the Rames, which Rares in strange colours, announcing tO the herds that the time for battle has come. All the Beastmen crowd around the circle in anticipation of the coming brawl. Each Bestigor and Champion has his hands tied behind his back, and the battle commences. By head-butting alone, one Beastman defeats all of his rivals, leaving their unconscious bodies lying in on that to no heaps the ground. The fact this Champion won comes surprise, for he bears the Mark ofKhorne. Nororious for his viciousness and cruelty, he makes a kill each day for his bloody master. 

With the Champion selected, the herd musters and sers forth to leave their lands in search of a new Herdsrone and to kill whatever they come upon along the way. Leading the Warherd is the marked Beastman Champion, the Shaman, and seven trusted Bestigor advisors. Following along are almost three dozen Beastmen of various strains, a Centigor, and a number ofTuskgors and Warhounds. Woe to any Human village that stands in their way.

###### **THE DARK TONGUE** 

The Dark Tongue, sometimes called the Black Speech, is the language of Chaos, spoken by its servancs and followers. It is the only language chat can adequately express the mysteries of Chaos, capturing the mystical and the arcane in ways chat no ocher language can. While similar in some ways co Daemonic-the magical language used for casting Chaos spells and rituals-Black Speech lacks the magical weight found in the ocher more blasphemous congue. Speaking the Dark Tongue does not (always) attract the attention of the Dark Gods, nor can it be used co speak the incantations needed co case a spell or recite a ritual. The Dark Tongue is also a root language for ochers spoken in the Old World and beyond. Queekish is ultimately a bastardisation of the Black Speech, polluted by mispronunciations and injected with squeaks, trills, and ocher sounds, since the Racmen lack the mouth structure co enunciate the words properly. Also, the Dark Elves ofNaggaroch speak a related language called Black Elven, which blends the lexicons of Elcharin (the congue of High Elves) and Black Speech, though they use pure Dark Tongue when discussing matters related co sorcery. 

_As_ mentioned, the Dark Tongue is rich in phrases and words chat express the complex nature of Chaos. Many make the mistake of attributing basic meanings co the words, but each holds far greater meaning and significance than a translation can supply. Each word encompasses a broad range of concepts, each with a different connotation depending on their arrangement with ocher words in the language and the addition of prefixes and suffixes, revealing different and deeper meanings held within the root. And, of course, mutating the root yields even more meanings. 

Though the individual words have incredible depth, there are far fewer words in the Black Speech than in many ocher languages, though the root mutations as well as the addition of prefixes and suffixes allow innumerable variations. Thus, few speakers of the Dark Tongue know the language fluendy or learn the many secrecs it hides. As a result, chis congue is an effective means of expression for occult lore. 

###### **CHAOS RUNES** 

When written, the Dark Tongue uses Chaos Runes. These inscriptions can be found in everything related co Chaos, from banners and the Chaos Monoliths chat demarcate the boundaries of the Chaos Wastes, co the hasty scratches on Herdscones, etching on weapons, and marks on shrines and temples, daubed in blood or dung. Chaos Runes are distinctive, readily identifiable for their character; there is no mistaking a Chaos Rune for anything ocher than what it is. 

###### **BEAST TONGUE** 

Like the Skaven, Beascmen have a difficult time forming the words of the Dark Tongue with their malformed bestial maws. _As_ a result, they use a crude mixture of Dark Tongue, body movemencs, gruncs, clicks, and pops, collectively called the Beast Tongue. This language sounds more like noise than a sophisticated congue, being not much more than an indescribable muttering and grumbling. Add co chis the shrieks, howls, and blears chat Beascmen use co punctuate and emphasise their phrases and there's considerable debate whether Beascmen speak a language at all. But regardless of prevailing opinions, Beascmen are an intelligent race, and despite their brutish aspect, and the face chat some of their kind cannot speak at all, they use their Tongue effectively, conveying a wide range of subjeccs and concepcs. 

###### **CHAOS RuNF.S As MARKERS** 

Chaos Runes represent ideas and experiences. In a sense, these Runes are shorthand for more complex phrases. A single Rune could represent a mutation or even mark a place of significant pools of _Dhar._ It's believed there's a single rune for every mutation, every change that has ever existed and will come co be. Many creatures blessed by the Dark Gods also discover these odd Runes pressing against their flesh from within. Hidden Mutants may cut these symbols out of their skin co preserve their cover. Hence, extensive scar tissue makes Witch Hunters suspicious. 

The Beast Tongue is beyond Mankind's ability co speak. In the rare instances when Beascmen deign co talk with Humans, they use a mix of basic Dark Tongue, body language, and gestures, only descending co Beast Tongue when frustrated, and killing the Human when really \ frustrated. 

###### **PHONETIC RuNF.S** 

###### **RuNF.S OF THE BEAST TONGUE** 

Chaos runes are represented by phonetic runes. These are used just like letters, forming words and phrases based on their arrangemencs. The runes are evolved from the Daemonic phonetic runes used in scribing spells and rituals. Such writings are highly sought in the Empire and beyond. Witch Hunters and ocher agencs of the cult of Sig mar seek co destroy these writings, while culciscs covet chem for the secrecs they contain. 

The Beascmen use a simplified form of the phonetic runes used in Dark Tongue co mark Herdscones or co leave messages for ocher members of their herd. These are always crude for Beascmen lack the precision needed co write clearly. Mose Beast men use their bodily wastes instead, finding the experience far more rewarding than **_"2lit_** caking the time co scribble something ;.~ - on a rock.

###### **THE TRUTH ABOUT WITCH HUNTERS** 

Feared and respected, loved and hated, Witch H unters are both the bane of civilisat ion and its salvation. Ruthless killers, they serve the interests 

**er IX: Defenders of the e Chapt Empir** 

of the Empire by putting torch co corruption wherever they find it. Anyone or anything they find chat is unnatural, they oppose. ###### **HISTORY** 

For nearly four hundred years, the Empire had languished in decline. Daemonologiscs, Necromancers, and cults were growing with startling frequency, and the Empire, such as it was, proved powerless co scop the spread. With a weak and ineffectual leader on the throne, the people turned co the cult of Sigmar for assistance. To meet the needs of the beleaguered provinces, Grand Theogonisc Siebold II formed the Order of the Silver Hammer: a group of Warrior-Priests and invescigacors, they were committed co ferreting out the agencs of Chaos. Armed with a leccer of commission with the seal of the Grand Theogonisc, they could reach anyone, anywhere. 

For the next sixty years, these Witch Hunters were not regarded as a significant threat, but they slowly expanded, building a network of spies and informants. Their reputation grew, and people began co fear their power. In response co the reckless destruction wrought by Daemonologiscs and Necromancers, the Grand Theogonisc authorised the Templars, as they were called, co use force in curbing the practice of all magic, ushering in a new era of brutal suppression of Wizards in all of their forms. 

With power comes corruption. The Witch Hunters expanded their chin ranks by accepting nearly anyone of religious dedication co join. And so, in the years chat followed, they recruited uncontrollable zealots and men of low character co aid in the fight against Chaos. And then the Grand Theogonisc dispatched the Templars to cleanse the sinful city of Mordheim. Believing the Sisters of Sigmar-che only order of Priestesses co serve Sigmar in any official capacity at chat time-co be heretics and corrupted by the evil in the city, the Grand Theogonist branded these women heretics and excommunicated chem from the cult. War raged for a year before a twin-tailed comet dropped from the heavens and wiped the City of the Damned from the map. 

Over the next three centuries, the Witch Hunters carried on as before, but the spread of Chaos proved coo great a threat for chem to contain. So terrible was the hold of the Ruinous Powers chat in 2111, the Grand Duke ofMiddenheim, who was also a Witch Hunter, had the entire town of Rocebach hanged, branding chem all worshippers of Chaos. This event outraged the ocher culcs, and chose of Ulric, Myrmidia, and ochers founded their own organisations to protect their congregations, though these never amounted co anything more than a few bands of poorly funded zealocs. 

However, in 2301, though, the world changed with the coming of Asavar Ku!, sparking the Great War Against Chaos. Once Magnus and his armies repulsed the horde, he was faced with reuniting an Empire chat had largely disintegrated over the previous centuries. To bring the unruly provinces back under the Imperial banner, he bound all Witch Hunters under the control of the Lord Protector. This man would answer co both the Emperor and the cult of Sigmar. By partially secularising the Witch Hunters, Magnus lessened any fears of an unchecked police force chat would condemn followers of ocher Gods to the same fiery deaths owed co Mutants and their ilk.

However, Magnus was arguably the lase strong Emperor for nearly two hundred years, and through the ineptness or ignorance of his successors, the Templars gradually slipped back to their old ways. Within a generation, the Order of Sigmar was burning and killing anyone it wished without regard to the law, and slipped from the emperor's control again. This continued until Volkmar von Hindenscern was selected to replace Grand Theogonisc Yorri XV. Through the efforts of purer members of the Templar order, corruption within the Witch Hunter organisation was revealed to Volkmar the Grim, who immediately cook control over the unruly and violent faction. Some whisper chat the Lord Protector's pose had been compromised by a hidden Cult chat was responsible for the widespread slaughter chat had gripped the Empire for years. Whatever the truth, the Grand Theogonisc dissolved the Lord Protector position and created three poses, tided General of the Sou ch, General of the North, and General of the Ease. These Witch Hunter Generals controlled their territories with an iron grip, dispatching Witch Hunters under their control to the dimmest reaches of the Empire. 

Once Magnus the Pious acknowledged the legitimacy of the Order of the Silver Hammer and bound it co the throne in addition co the Grand Theogonisc, he made the Witch Hunters the official scare-sanctioned and funded inquisitors of the Empire. This granted the Witch Hunters considerable power, placing chem above their rivals in ocher Culcs. Though they have incredible authority, they are now bound by the law and muse work within its boundaries. Witch Hunters are no longer free co burn at will. Now, they may arrest any Imperial citizen they suspect to be guilty of consorting with Chaos. They also have the right to interrogate the suspect, using torture if needed. And if they can gain a confession, they are within their righcs to burn the suspect at once. Otherwise, they muse cry the accused in front of a jury of their peers. But since there are no laws governing evidence, the Witch Hunter is free co use any technique he wishes to convince the jury of the suspecc's guile. In almost all cases, the Witch Hunter wins. 

###### **OrHER WITCH HUNTERS** 

When one chinks of a Witch Hunter, two thoughts come co mind: The Templars of Sigmar; and the secular, provincial Witch Hunters. Boch groups are hardened veterans driven by their commitment co the extermination of Chaos. However, there are many ochers who hunt down Mutants and their ilk. 

Official Witch Hunters look down on chose who practice their trade without authorisation from the cult of Sigmar. The reason is simple: Hunting Mutancs and their kind often requires breaking the law, creating more problems than they solve, unless protocols are observed. Furthermore, without the special training Witch Hunters receive, the independencs are more susceptible to Chaos and ics corruption. Far coo many come to believe the couch of the Dark Gods reaches all things, leading chem to burn innocencs out of some misplaced sense of justice. As a result, if caught impersonating a Witch Hunter, the subject always faces death. 

###### **MER.CENARIE.5** 

The most common Witch Hunter is the mercenary. A sell-sword, he uses his talents for combat to remove dangers from a community. Though they kill Mutancs, they are not as rigorous in their efforcs as legitimate Witch Hunters are, and moreover, they are prone co corruption and bribery. 

###### **RENEGADES** 

Beside the common mercenary and the sanctioned Witch Hunters, there is a growing new breed of Hunters chat aren't driven by gold, faith, or Imperial Law. These individuals hunt agencs of Chaos for reasons of their own-guilt, hate, revenge, and so on. While they have the zeal of the cult-sponsored organisation, they lack the infrastructure and support to help chem overcome their foes. As a result, many of these men find a grim end, overwhelmed by their enemies. But a few, a scant few, make their mark and earn the respect of their peers with their impossible successes.

###### **WITCH HUNTER TACI'ICS** 

Mose see Witch Hunters as nothing more than state- or Cult-sanctioned agitators, who control crowds by spreading fear and suspicion, and there is some truth co chis. Witch Hunters use the resources available in a community, appropriating local soldiers and militia co help with whatever threat they face. Failing the presence of competent guards, they'll make use of the peasants if they muse. 

Usually, such open activity comes lace in their investigation. Witch Hunters don't capture their prey unless they are patient and have all of their faces first. So unless the threat is immediately obvious, the Hunter will snoop around the community, looking for suspicious behaviour and clues. During chis time, he assembles a group of helpers, locals who know the people and the ins and outs of the community. From chis assistance, he can gauge their purity by keeping chem close at hand. Witch Hunters will often "befriend" a suspect co keep a close eye on chem. Once the corruption is exposed, the Witch Hunter enlists the rest of the cown through fear co help bring down the offending Mutants or culciscs. Then, once captured, the Witch Hunter interrogates, using torture if necessary co cease out the information he needs and co expose any accomplices. Those captives who don't die from interrogation are cleansed by fire, and anyone who assisted chem is either tortured or ki lled publicly co deter anyone else from aiding the agents of Chaos. 

###### **WITCH HUNTER ADVENTURES** 

A Witch Hunter campaign can be an intensely rewarding experience, caking characters inco the most dangerous and despicable places in the Empire. Whether hunting Mutants, thwarting and exposing cults, or cracking down and killing Beascmen, there are plenty of opportunities for adventure. Furthermore, because Witch Hunters face a multitude of foes, these campaigns can be tailored co the play styles of nearly any group. 

###### **~~Combat~~** 

The most obvious campaign style is the combat-oriented campaign. Opposing Beascmen and Mutants places Witch Hunters in constant danger, and a good thrilling combat always waits in the wings. Since the agents of Chaos are many and varied, there's no chance of running out of interesting encounters. 

###### **~~n~~ Exploratio**

An Exploration campaign allows you co vividly describe the Empire, caking the adventurers co the most far-flung places in their quest. 

###### **~~e~~ Intrigu** 

Corruption is everywhere, even amongst the Witch Hunters. The temptations sec forth by the Ruinous Powers attract even the most stalwart members. Furthermore, since they muse face the agents of Chaos, they often risk contracting the corruption themselves and bringing back their wickedness co their organisation. ###### **THE RITUAL OF ExoRCISM** 

This phase lasts ldl0/5 hours. During this time, all mortals witnessing the ritual must make Challenging (-10%) Will Power Tests (if not harder if the scene is especially grotesque). Those who fail gain (ld 10+2)/4 Insanity Points. Exorcists, Priests of Sigmar, and Witch Hunters reduce the difficulty of this test by one or more steps depending on whether or not they have performed an exorcism before. 

When faced with a possessed mortal, more often than not it is coo late to help the subject, and it falls to ochers co destroy the vessel and send the Daemon back to the Realm of Chaos. However, in some instances, the Daemon has not yet devoured the mind of the subject, and a trained Priest can remove the offending spirit through magical means. 

_A Chorus of Evils._ Next, the Daemon's voice becomes a torrent of words, always offensive, often nonsensical. The exorcism cannot continue until the Daemon is silenced. This can be achieved with a simple trick. More powerful Daemons require a little more effort to quieten. In extreme cases, the Exorcist may be forced co cut the tongue from the victim. Regardless, the Exorcist and Daemon make a second opposed Will Power Test, and if successful, the Exorcist may move onto the next stage. Otherwise, he must start again in twenty-four hours. 

_Sigmar's Heirs_ presencs a new spell called Exorcism. A Lesser Spell, it is available to Priescs of any religion. Exorcism is useful for removing spiritual contamination or possession by ghos tly beings and even a few minor fiends, but it is insufficient co deal with most Daemons. 

###### **~~The Rirual of Exorc;ism~~** 

**Type:** Divine 

**Arcane Language:** Magick **Magic:** 2 

• _'ITTir ofWills._ Once the Daemon falls silent, a palpable presence descends in the immediate area. At this time, the Daemon and the Exorcist wage war for the host. The Exorcist forces the Daemon to reveal more about itself and establishes a firm control. At this point, the Exorcist makes his Casting Roll. If he succeeds, he and the Daemon make their final opposed Will Power Tests. If the Daemon wins, the Exorcist must begin anew in twenty-four hours. Otherwise, the Daemon flees the host. 

**XP:** 300 

- **Ingredients:** An illuminated copy of _The Book of Sigmar,_ the sign of the hammer or twin-tailed comet, new Priestly vestments, rope and nails for binding, a vial of holy water, a hammer, a goat (or some ocher animal) or mirror, and a roaring fire. 

- **Conditions:** The Exorcist must spend three consecutive days prior to casting the ritual in meditation and prayer. Once he is finished, he gathers his witnesses, one co see and watch, one co help, and at lease one who is bound to the victim by blood or marriage. The helpers must bind the victim to a tree with stout rope and nails, while the Exorcist readies the animal (or mirror) to contain the fiendish entity. 

• _The Casting Out of the Possessing Spirit-._ Assuming the Exorcist defeats the Daemon, the entity flees the hose's body for the Realm of Chaos. Its passage is manifest, and all experience its flight. In some circumstances, there is a rush of sound as the thing escapes. If the time of possession was shore, the host resumes control over his body with little to no recollection of what transpired. Most, though, do not emerge &om this experience unscathed. Aside from physical injuries caused by the Daemon, there are psychic scars, and madness is often a res ult. Characters who survive the exorcism automatically gain at least 1 Insanity Point, though, as can be seen under **Possessed Characters** in **Chapter** II: **The Lost and the Damned,** they can gain more. 

- **Consequences:** If the Casting Roll fails, the possessing Daemon gains a + 10% bonus to all Tests made to resist future _Rituals of Exorcism._ The bonus is cumulative. In addition, all characters present must succeed on a Hard (-20%) Will Power Test or gain ldl0/2 Insanity Points from the horror of the experience. 

   - If the Casting Roll results in Tzeentch's Curse, the caster becomes 

   - possessed instead. 

**Casting Number:** 13 

**Casting Time:** 8 hours or more 

- **Description:** The _Ritual of Exorcism_ incorporates five basic steps, which can be role-played if the GM and players wish. 

- _Dispelling the Faf'ade:_ At this stage, the Daemon hides within the host as if it's not there at all. Whilst it retains complete control over the mortal's body, its movements are natural as is its speech. The Exorcist must reveal the Daemon and learn its nature. This is often the hardest pare of the exorcism since the Daemon is not cooperative. Furthermore, the Exorcist must be vigilant and resist the temptation to engage in unnecessary conversation. For the exorcism to work, the Exorcist must be firm in his resolve and committed co the effort with all authority granted to him by Sigmar.

the sky. They are always crafted from the finest of materials-the most treasured being exotic crystalline rocks with pink or purple streaks and glittering veins of quartz. Rumours abound oflarge Monoliths crafted from a single, huge gemstone, but they are rarely seen. These monuments are inevitably carved with figures of Daemons, animals, and Humans in unlikely and blasphemous positions. These images are beguiling and repulsive at the same time, conjuring up images of seductive power and pleasure, entrancing music, excessive feasts, and other temptations of Chaos. Graven with verse from long-dead poecs, these words can mesmerise and delude the weak-minded, forcing them to relish the careful turn of phrase, co inspect the gentle Aow of thought co form and back again, and to spend eternity mulling on the dreams of pleasure and pain evoked by the throbbing stone. 

###### MoNOLlTHs TO TZEENTa-I 

No two Monoliths dedicated to Tzeentch are alike, and trying co describe them with any consistency is almost impossible. Some may be made from exotic scone like black obsidian or glowing marble, although almost any other substance may be used. Even then, these Monoliths change and 



warp over the years co suit the whims ofTzeentch and his followers. Tales persist of Monoliths formed in living fire, cascades of water, or columns of solid smoke. A few are even unmoored from the land, Aoating low in the sky, or inexplicably sitting on the surface of a lake or river. 

###### UsING MoNOLlTHs 

Anyone that reads the blasphemous runes of a Chaos Monolith must make a Hard (-20%) Will Power Test or gain ldl0/2 Insanity Poincs. Monoliths are coveted and feared as being raw sources of magical energy. All spellcasters that cast spells within 100 feet of a Monolith add + 1d10 to their Casting Rolls-this includes all spells, including those with seemingly good intent, such as healing magic). However, using this energy comes with great risk. _Any_ failure to cast a spell resulcs in a Catastrophic Chaos Manifestation (see **Appendix** II: **Tzeentch's Curse Expanded).** 

Monoliths dedicated co Khorne, however, act as siphons co magic-the Blood God despises the use of magic. All spells cast within 100 feet of these Chaos Monoliths fail automatically, resulting in a Catastrophic Chaos Manifestation. Monoliths are incredibly cough, but not indestructible. A band armed with picks and hammers could eventually reduce one co rubble, if they were brave and strong-willed enough co stay there that long. Regardless of the material they are made of, all monoliths are treated as having a 10 Toughness Bonus and 500 Wounds. Monoliths seem to "know" when they are purposefully being assaulted. For every 50 Wounds the Monolith sustains, it summons a Lesser Daemon of the appropriate type to deal with the attackers. These Daemons emerge from the Monolith icself and attack the nearest person-they never retreat, and they fight until destroyed. 

###### **CHANGE STORMS** 

The weather is unpredictable enough, but the Winds of Chaos sometimes make it horrible and capricious beyond compare. During times when the veil between the Old World and the Realm of Chaos is thin, the weather often heralds terrible times ahead. Change Scorms are bizarre manifestations of Chaos in the form of dangerous winds, disgusting rain, and stranger things. 

Change Storms are most common in the Chaos Wastes, though strange weather sometimes appears in every part of the Old World. Unholy sites (particularly around Monoliths, combs, or the Temples of Chaos Gods) sometimes assist in manifesting these scorms. At the GM's discretion, a Change Storm occurs, and he can either roll on the table below or pick one effect. These conditions last for 1 dl 0 minutes and typically cover an area up co a mile in diameter with the effects described below. 

###### **Acidic Precipitatio** **~~n~~** 

The sky breaks open, pouring down a torrent of thick, oily rain, snow, or sleet that burns whatever it couches. For each minute a Character remains in the acidic precipitation, he must succeed on a Toughness Test or take a Damage 2 hit. 

###### **Reverse** **<u>e</u> Temperatur** 

The temperature in the area switches suddenly to the opposite of what is normal. For example, if the Scorm occurs during the middle of summer, the temperature drops below freezing and stares snowing. If the Scorm occurs in the winter, the temperature rises co a scorching summer heat. If the temperature is moderate, there is a 50% chance of either effect occurring. 

###### **~~Wind of Madness~~** 

Powerful, mind-shattering and soul-rending winds tumble out from the north, scouring the land and driving all mad who hear them. For every minute a Character remains exposed in this harsh scorm, he must succeed on a Challenging (-10%) Will Power Test or gain 1 Insanity Point. 

###### **<u>Rain of Creatures</u>** 

A shower of tiny creatures, typically frogs, fish, foetal pigs, and the like, suddenly spills down on the area. The rain causes no damage, but witnesses must succeed on a Will Power Test or gain 1 Insanity Point. Most of the creatures are dead on landing, but some survive and slowly limp about until they expire. Anyone unwise enough co closely examine any of the creatures finds them rotted, deformed, and rife with mutations. 

###### **~~Hail of Fire~~** 

A powerful scorm of flaming hail bombards the area. Characters exposed and out in the open must make a Toughness Test each minute or take a Damage 3 hit and risk the chance of catching on fire (see _WFRP_ page 136).

###### **~~Rain of Blood~~** 

A torrent of tainted blood rains down from diseased, crimson clouds. Anyone exposed tO this rain must succeed on a Toughness Test or contract contract The Bloody Flux or the Green Pox (see WFRPpage 136). 

###### **Aethyric Wind** 

What begins as a light gust filled with motes of multi-coloured lighrs picks up speed and becomes a gale carrying the raw stuff of Chaos. Anyone caught in the area must make a Willpower Test every two minutes or suffer from the effects of a Minor Chaos Manifestation (see **Appendix II: Tzeentch's Curse Expanded).** The result affects even nonspellcasters (who can ignore wholly magical effects-a small blessing). 

###### **ENCOUNTERS IN THE CHAOS W ASTB** 

The Chaos Wastes contain horrors more likely to be found in nightmares than the real world. Although seemingly empty, the Chaos Wastes teem with terrible creatures, marauding hordes, and unholy sites for anyone unlucky or foolish enough to find himself there. The Chaos Wastes are home to untold numbers ofBeastmen, Goblin tribes, Ore hordes, and Daemons of all sires and power. Roving bands of crazed Humans prowl the wastes-some are aligned with a specific Chaos God, while others are merely servanrs of Chaos in irs purest form. The most dangerous are Chaos Warriors, fearsome Champions that have received additional "blessings" from their Gods. 

**Table 10-3: Encounters in the Chaos Wastes** shows typical creatures that might be encountered in the Chaos Waste. If required, the GM may may roll on the Aspect of Chaos chart tO determine which faction the creature or creatures claim allegiance (ignore inappropriate rolls). 

ago. The srory irself is a myth, and few believe it, though the lure of wealth and plunder is too much tO resist for some. In truth, the vision of the city in its splendour is merely an illusion, created by a Chaos Sorcerer and his followers to lure the foolish tO their death. However, the forgotten, crumbling remains of Gultberg do indeed lay hidden beneath this veil of deceit, and who can say what hides there? 

###### **AnVENTURB IN THE CHAOS W ASTB** 

The Chaos Wastes are rife with potential adventures of all sorts. Lost and forgotten cities lay waiting to be plundered. Hordes of terrible beasrs, Daemons, and men wander its length and breadth. Both the brave and foolish dream of entering the Chaos Wastes in search of gold, plunder, and adventure. A few even return, often with little treasure and with horrible tales. 

###### **~~Adventure Hook; The Hidden FoureS-5~~** 

A young, brash nobleman named William Neuner has recently returned tO Altdorf after a disastrous adventure into the Chaos Wastes. The only one of his group to return, Neuner is now hopelessly insane and raves endlessly about his companions being held captive in a fortress made of bone, brass, and iron. He reveals that his group was beset by a company of Beastmen, but he can give no reasoning why he and his companions were not immediately killed and eaten. His family believes the only relief that can be provided to their son and heir is a mission to the Chaos Wastes to rescue his companions, destroy the foul Beascmen, or both. They are wi lling tO pay handsomely for fools who would undertake such **a** task. 

###### **~~Adventure Hook; $.1crifice in the Snow~~** 

Klaus Reinfrank, a rich and eccentric merchant lord from Talabheim, has hired a caravan tO take a precious, but secretive, cargo tO Erengrad. Unbeknownst to anyone, Reinfrank has been slowly corrupted by the Lord of Change and has been granted visions of unimaginable wealth and power if proper sacrifice is made tO Tzeentch. _As_ the caravan enters inro the open steppes ofKislev, Reinfrank insisrs on taking an unexplored route, claiming he has a map that shows a shortcut tO avoid the worst terrain. In truth, Reinfrank intends tO lead the caravan to a shrine sacred tO his Chaos Lord and sacrifice his treasure and the men he hired to gain the favour he craves. 

###### **Adventure Hook; Death Comes on Icy Wing** **~~s~~** 

Deep in the tundra of the Chaos Wastes, a Sorceress of Nurgle located an enormous corpse of some mysterious creature frozen in the permafrost. Although she has no idea what the thing was in life, its body contains the remnants of a strange, terrible disease. Seeing it as a true blessing from the Plague Lord, the Sorceress has partially thawed the body out and summoned a huge murder of carrion crows to feast upon irs decayed Aesh. These mutated birds travel far and wide, spreading the new disease tO the thorps and settlemenrs of Kislev, Norsca, and even as far as the northern reaches of the Empire. 

###### **Adventure Hook; City of Decei** **~~t~~** 

Rumours persist of a glittering city somewhere along the shores of the Sea of Claws. Norse traders claim this is possibly Gultberg, a rich and proud settlement purportedly swallowed up by the Waste unrold generations

###### **-XAVIER PFAFF, MlDDENHEIM HISTORIAN** 

_''They say the Norsemen worship strange and bloodthirsty Gods that demand Human sacrifice, perpetual warfare, and the conquest of the soft lands. That's rubbish, I always say. ###### **THE LAND** 

There are many reasons not co make the journey co the lands of the Norsemen. It is difficult, dangerous, and rarely worth the risk. Norsca is every bit the inhospitable place Old Worlders chink. Thanks co its latitude, about half the year is a dim twilight, with the sun nothing more than a faint disk hovering just below the horizon, shedding its feeble light across the land. The temperatures are continually below freezing, clutching the mountains in a frozen grasp. Snow falls almost constantly, worsened by the icy spray blown by the winds over the Sea of Chaos. ###### **GEOGRAPHY** 

**_"T'ain't nothing but mountains and more mountains ... "_** 

###### -MIKEL K RAUS, M ERCENAR y 

Norsca is famous for ics daunting mountains. Bordered on all sides by these magnificent peaks, travel inco the heartland borders on the impossible. Mose travellers keep co the sparse, fortified villages dotting the southern and western coastlines. The mountains themselves are steeped in local myth, often named for the legendary giancs and icy fortresses on the peaks, such as the Mountains ofThjazi and the Jocunheims. Although the mountains dominate the terrain, it is false co say they are all there is ofNorsca. This harsh land is also home co dense forescs of spruce and pine, mostly blanketing the interior slopes where they are protected from the worse storms descending from the north. 

In addition co the dense forests and high mountains, Norsca also has glacial seas chat screech down from the Chaos Wastes, forming the Frozen Sea co the northeast. These massive ice fields are responsible for the jagged mountains forming the northernmost boundaries chat offer some shelter from the changing forces occasionally blowing south from the chaotic north. During the summer months, the air warms just enough co drain the land and enliven the few screeches of plains chat serve co supplement the Norsemen's diet of fish and bear meat. 

Given the climate and the unforgiving peaks, any attempcs co map chis land have met with failure. There are simply coo many defiles and gorges, coo many peaks and darkened forescs, all of which contain things changed by the loosed energies of Chaos. At most, the people of the Empire have a vague idea of chis land's shape and a sense of what lies within, but any particulars are merely conjecture.

###### **THENoueMN<N** 

Despite the claims of many Imperial hiscorians, the twelve tribes chat would one day form the Empire were not the first men co occupy the Old World. The Tileans, Escalians, Breconnians, and even the peoples of Araby and ancient Khemri have held portions of what would become the Empire. Ocher kingdoms rose and fell, leaving behind the ruins of their civilisations. Among these people, there was a race of Humans who held the lands north of the Forest of Shadows, a tribe now called the Norsii. Large, well-formed, and nomadic, they lived from harvesting the bounty of the seas, hunting in the woods, and eating what they could coax from the ground through crude farming techniques. Never populous, they remained content in their lives, worshipping their strange Gods and following stranger customs.

###### **- H AUBR, N ORSEMAN** 

Norsemen as a cohesive people do not exist. The name means "men of the north," and it is a term used by Old Worlders co collectively define the various tribes that occupy Norsca. Within each tribal group there are important differences that make each unique, with particular customs and beliefs co set chem apart from the ocher men of their country. 

###### **IDENTIFYING THE NORSE** 

The Norsii's peace was disturbed when ocher tribes boiled into the Reik Basin. The worst of these was the tribe called the Teucogens. They were warlike and murderous, and swept across the land like an axe-wielding tidal wave. The Norsii people were forced co take up arms and fight for their lives. All coo quickly, they were pushed back from their lands and forced eastwards into conRicc with ocher tribes, including the Udoses and the Ungols. Many minor conRiccs ensued, but, eventually, an uneasy peace descended, and the Norsii seeded again; although, this time with weapons ready. One of the principal difficulties they now faced revolved around the differing religious beliefs. The nearby tribes mostly venerated Ulric and Taal, the Gods of the Teutogens and the Taleutens, while the Norsii worshipped primal forces of blood, death, and, more importantly, their ancescors. The challenges of their opposing faiths, as well as the Norsii's savage ways, put chem at odds with the ocher tribes. The land was not big enough for all, so, eventually, a trickle of Norsii began co leave their hunting grounds co find a safe harbour elsewhere in the north. 

Norsemen are a distinctive race; they have large frames and are extremely muscular. They have the pale skin of the men of the Empire, but are taller and stronger. Norsemen tend co be fair-haired-blond and red being the most common. All wear their hair long, keeping it in braids, and sometimes weaving feathers or beads in the knocs. The Norsemen don furs and hides as armour, though some have taken co wearing the mail of their southern kin. 

###### **ORIGINS OF THE NORSEMEN** 

There are many ridiculous beliefs regarding the origins of these people. Some claim they are the spawn of Man and Daemon, creatures whose very nature is at odds with the natural order. Ochers claim the Norsemen are descendancs of Giants, kin co the foul creatures of the Ogre Kingdoms. Some have gone so far as co claim Norseman are creatures of snow and ice, as unforgiving as the winter winds. But the truth, as shaded by myth and legend as it is, is far less fantastic. 

The Greenskin races had long proved problematic for the people of the Old World. Their constant raiding weakened the tribes of Men, and even troubled the fortress holds of the Dwarfs. When Sigmar emerged as chief of the Unberogen tribe, he brought together twelve ocher tribes under his banner through diplomacy and war, even conquering the warlike Teutogens. Once united, he led the tribes co face the Ores and Goblins, and pushed chem from his lands. When he was finished, he forged the tribes inco a new Empire co bind all co his vision of the future. 



However, not all were content to swear their allegiance co what they saw as a lucky, albeit brave, warlord. Those who would not submit co Sigmar's rule were forced from the newborn Empire co find homes in ocher lands. The remaining members of the Norsii, along with the disaffected members of the ocher tribes, Red the Empire, heading north. However, these lands were populated by the Ungols, who were not pleased co have refuges in their lands, and forced the Reeing tribesmen further north still, into the frozen, ice-choked mountains; the land now known as Norsca. 

More and more people Red co Norsca, and there they found the descendants of the early emigrancs who had largely embraced darker aspeccs of their primitive beliefs. This new land was dangerous and harsh, and the death coll was high from the environment as well as from the depredations by the roaming bands of Kurgan who wandered down from the Chaos Wastes even further north. Added co this new mix of peoples were strange men, believed co be kin to chose who were changed into Beastmen in the earliest days of Mankind. It was from this clash of cultures and races that a new people were born: the Norse. 

###### **THE NORSEMEN** 

###### **AND THE OLD WoRLD** 

Since the earliest migrations, the Norsemen have retained a strange relationship with the rest of the Old World. They straddle the line that divides the bloodthirsty hordes of Chaos that lie in the Shadowlands

from the huddled masses who fight to defend their homes and way of life from the Incursions of Chaos. In short: To the Empire, the Norsemen are antagonises, sometime allies, and explorers.

###### **NORSEMEN AS ANTAGONISTS** 

###### **NORSEMEN AS EXPLORERS** 

The most common encounter between the O ld Worlder and Norseman is in battle. Norsca is not a land renowned for its food and comfort; it is a place of violence and scarcity. When the Norsemen's population increases beyond their capacity to feed themselves, they set out to raid settlements along the Imperial and Breconnia's coastlines, sacking the small cowns they find and carrying off livestock, grains, and new slaves. Depending on the need, the Norsemen have attacked Erengrad and Marienburg, though both cities boast defences enough co repel all but the largest attacks. More often than not, when a Norse fleet approaches a community, they offer to take foodstuffs and booty in exchange for not burning the community to the ground. Though it may mean starvation through the winter, many Old Worlders give up a portion of their foodstuffs and even a child or two to ensure they have a chance to make it through to the next season. 

As some of the oldest seafaring Humans in the O ld World, Norsemen are at home amidst the waves and the spray of salt water. They are master shipbuilders, capable of constructing sleek ships famous for their speed and durability. They have a keen sense for navigation, can read the stars, and have a natural wanderlust that carries them across the oceans. It's true they undertake some voyages out of curiosity or because they were instructed to do so to appease the Gods, but most are opportunities for warriors co prove their mettle in battle against whatever new enemies they encounter. And if they acquire new thralls, weapons, gold, and silver, even better. 

It's believed there's nowhere in all the world the Norsemen have not travelled. Legends tell of courageous seamen crossing the Great Ocean to found colonies in far-flung Lustria, or to wage war against the foul Dark Elves. There are tales among the Norse of crossing the Sea of Chaos co reach the lands of the Hung, co battle the treacherous Chaos Marauders and bring back untold treasures. Merchants travelling the Silk Road make mention of blond giants amidst the cultured people of fabled Cathay and Nippon. While these tales spark the imagination, who can say if they are true or not? Still, the Norsemen have great confidence in their skills at sea, and point co Losteriksson, who was the first Old Worlder co set foot on the shores of Lustria and live co record the event. There, he founded Skeggi-named for his daughter who was the first Norse child born in the New World. 

Many Norsemen attack the Empire and other communities out of spite. Long have the Norsemen believed their lands were taken from them by Sigmar and his allies, so each raid pays back a little more of the debt they feel the O ld Worlders owe. To make matters worse, they also find the Imperials lacking in courage and skill, hearkening co soft Gods, and lacking in honour. For them, it is their duty to purge the land of such weak men and pave the way for the Incursion that will mark the final and glorious end co all things. 

Raiding is also a part oflife. Among the Norse, a man gains honour simply by being a warrior. Excellence in fighting not only honours the Norsemen but also brings honour to all of their forbears. As a result, young men raid coastal villages as a means to prove themselves, and many are goaded co greater acts of daring by their Jarls-the lords of the Norse are well aware that ambitious young warriors grow up into restive, dangerous, ambitious, experienced warriors. 

###### **NORSEMEN SOCIETY** 

Despite legends to the contrary, Norsca is not an organised nation, but rather a collection of petty states ruled by warlords, although even "state" is perhaps coo strong of a term. In actuality, Norsca is loosely divided inco different territories held by each of the seven dominant tribes. Within each, there are dozens of smaller communities that comprise one to three family clans who swear fealty co their tribe's King. Though nominally similar in structure and settlement patterns, there is a marked split between the Norsemen of this land. 

Finally, Norsemen attack other setdemencs because they are compelled to by their Gods. From time to time, the Seers receive visions that they interpret as invocations co war. The black Winds of Chaos blow south, pushing the Kurgan inco Norsca and forcing the Norsemen to venture south to avoid being devoured or sacrificed on the bloody altars of their cousins.

The ideal person in Norscan culture is the young, virile slayer. He's courageous, skilled, and cough. He is the warrior. He is the hunter, the defender, the raider, and the hero. Becoming a warrior is, at heart, a simple matter. Anyone can pick up a sword and fight. The life of a warrior is often brief, but it is always exciting. Between raids, these men provide flesh for the clan by hunting the wild beascs of Norsca. They gain prestige when they return with an ice boar, moose, or some massive shark pulled from the seas. These fights are rarely lethal since killing a warrior in times of peace is a grave crime. 

###### **NORSEMEN SETTLEMENTS** 

In order for a city to thrive and grow, it must have substantial farmland and natural resources. Considering the harsh climate and the rugged terrain, Norsca cannot support the same sized setdemencs the Empire can. Instead, the Norsemen congregate in small communities consisting of three co five families scattered throughout the territory controlled by their tribe. Each community is led by a Jar! who is often advised by a Seer or Vicki and propped up by a cadre ofloyal warriors. Certainly, there are larger and smaller setdemencs, with the bigger ones being held by the tribe's King and the smaller ones struggling co survive until they are eventually wiped out by the elemencs, a rival tribe, or some man-eating horror. 

To the outsider, Norsemen warriors are all the same: bloodthirsty bands of killers. But there are distinctions even among the various clans. Loyalty co a particular Jar! engenders peculiarities that all his bonded warriors embrace. Some warriors have a particular fighting style, perhaps using only axes, or fighting with shields whose edges are sharpened to a razor edge. Others are incredible leapers, while some wear armour only on the froncs of their bodies so they may never retreat. Unusual haircucs, copknocs, a particular braid of beard, or lack of a beard altogether characterise the differing groups of Norsemen. 

###### **SITE.5** 

When selecting a new site for a settlement, Norsemen have three things in mind. First, the site must have access to a resource: good fishing, forests for timber, or an area of rich soil suitable for farming. Second, the settlement must be defensible; areas nestled in the mountains or hidden in dense forest are preferable. The last consideration is the ability co see in all directions. What good is a village nestled in a gorge of the mountains if one cannot see the approach of one's enemies? To make otherwise unsuitable sites useful, the Norsemen construct watchtowers co holding piles of wood drenched in oil co serve as a signal fire for the nearby community. These watchcowers may serve one or more setdemencs, and should the tribe fall under an attack, the signal fires can erupt all over the territory, calling the Jarls to muster their warriors and make ready for war. 

###### **_Seers_ and Vitki** 

Seers advise the Jarls in matters pertaining to the will of their ancestors and the Gods. It falls to these privileged men (and occasionally women) to interpret the movemencs of the Winds of Magic, the whispers of Daemons, and the spirics of fal len warriors to guide the Jar! co choose the proper course for the tribe. Vicki fulfil a role similar to the Seers, but are steeped in the arcane traditions of the Ruinous Powers. Many advisors in service to the Norsemen tribes are former cultiscs, forced co _Ree_ their native lands after being uncovered by the Witch Hunters. These individuals are highly regarded, and are valued members of their adopted communities. With a word, a Vicki can order any peasant's death, and thralls die by the scores to fuel the dark magic needed to perform their profane rituals. 

###### **STRUCTURES** 

Norsemen architecture is built with utility as the forefront concern. A structure must be warm and big enough co accommodate a large family. Also, these structures should be low co the ground so the falling snow can conceal the structures from predators. In the spring and summer, their roofa are seeded with grass so they blend in with the surrounding land. 

###### **Jarls** 

The Jar! is a great warrior loyal co the tribe's King. In exchange for his devoted service, the King grants the Jar! hunting grounds, warriors, treasure, and thralls. The Jar! is the absolute lord of his lands but is expected to be subservient to his master, and when the winds of war blow, the Jar! is expected co come to the aid of his King, and lend his warriors for the cause. Should the King or Queen die without an heir, the Jarls fight a bloody contest to take the throne. 

Most structures in these setdemencs are longhouses: long and large, single-storied buildings covered in thatched roofs. Most have some additional adornment, featuring whorls and knots and working in beautifully carved images of Dragons and ocher mythological creatures. Within the longhouses, there's a central common room where meals are cooked, Skalds tell tales of the Gods and ancestors, and most of the family sleeps for warmth. Ocher areas attached co the common room serve as storage, private bedrooms, or as pens to hold animals. 

Whilst it's expected that Jarls be utterly loyal to their monarch, it's not unheard of for a Jar! to slay his master and usurp his position. Such a coup is always dangerous since it invites reprisals and further treachery. But in times of weak leaders, it is expected for a Jar! to step up and seize power. 

Thralls live in hovels, little more than a collection of stitched-together skins hanging on a wooden frame. To keep out the cold, the slaves smear mud or excrement on the walls. The thralls are free to come and go as they please, as the Norsemen know there is nowhere for their captives co run. The Norsemen may sacrifice their slaves, but at least it's a quick death-something not often found in the trackless wilds ofNorsca. 

###### **Kings** 

The most powerful Norseman in every tribe is the King. Most Kings were once Jarls, but occasionally, one inherits the tide from his father. Rules of succession vary a great deal. In the north, the tribal leader is always the viccor of a bloody contest, with all claimancs battling for control. In the south, Kings inherit their tid es in a way similar to those used in the Empire. Most Kings bear the favour of their God, having a potent Mark of Chaos to show their right to rule. Celebrated Chaos Champions, they prove their worth and might in war time and again. 

Each community has a holy site of some kind. Mose are caves burrowed inco the side of a hill or mountain, but a few are freestanding structures. Such sites can be identified by the altar and bonfires, mounds of skulls, and sacrifices of plunder. Strange runes mark the entryways, forbidding all those who are not blooded warriors from entering, but even the most but even the most even the most courageous fighter fears what lies within. ###### **INDUSTRY**

###### **BATTLE**

And so warriors occupy a place of honour amongst the Norse, for it is they who have the chance to receive the rewards awaiting them in death. ###### **NoRsE Cut TURE**

Aside from a disturbing obsession with death, the Norsemen have a strange assortment of practices that damn them in the eyes of many O ld Worlders. Ranging from the curious to the downright disgusting, the manner and nature of these customs largely depends on the tribe. 

###### **Battle Customs** 

The sacrifice of thralls is by and large the most common act prior to battle, but it is by no means the only cuscom. Since death in battle is the ideal fate for any warrior, women in Norsca are forbidden to mourn che loss of their husbands and sons. ###### **CAREERS** 

This chapter presencs new Basic and Advanced Careers. They are presented in alphabetical order. 

###### **~~Bondsman~~** 

The Bondsman is a warrior in service to a particular Jar!. He is expected co live in the Jarl's Hall, share the Jarl's food, and be steadfastly loyal. In exchange for his pledge of loyalty, the Jar! rewards service with gifcs, such as weapons and armour, and to the very best, land and tide. The worth of the gift is never measured in actual value, but rather the prestige it bescows on the Bondsman. It's important co remember such gifcs do not make the Bondsman a mercenary; rather, it is a reward for constant and loyal service.

###### **~~Freeholder~~** 

One of the greatest rewards a Jar! may grant to his Bondsmen and loyal Peasants is land. Upon gaining property, these men and women are accorded a special status. For those who were not warriors, they have the same status as Bondsmen. For those who were once warriors, land is usually a gift given in exchange for lengthy and valued service. Many Freeholders eventually become Jarls if selected by their King. Otherwise, they gain a piece of land and a number of Thralls to work it.

celebrated traits. The most powerful warrior of the tribe is called the Zar, led the Zar, their name for the Chieftain. He holds his position by dine of his power, his power, the favour of his divine master, and the loyalty of his warriors, which he earns by bestowing onco chem gifts for their service. Facial scarring is the clearest sign of a Zar's ability, and once a battle is won, the Shaman (a Chaos Sorcerer) makes an incision on the leader's cheek. 

Beneath the Zar are his bold and savage warriors chat live co fight. After co fight. After fight. Gold, silver, and ocher precious metals are melted down and formed inco arm rings. He with the with the the most rings has achieved the most victories and is greatly respected and feared by the rest of his tribe. 

When not waging war, the warriors serve the rest of the tribe as as hunters. They ride off into the steppes co bring down antelope and wild cattle co ld cattle co co feed the rest of the tribe. This is also an opportunity for a warrior co prove himself co his kin, and often times, Spawn and ocher creatures are brought back for great feasts. Noc only do these efforts feed the tribe, but they also they also keep the warrior's skills sharp for when he is called co battle. 

###### **SLAVES** 

The Kurgan are also notorious slavers. As pare of the battle's spoils, they collect the survivors and caccoo chem on the face with the marks marks of a particular Zar. The ink used almost always includes some amount of Warpscone co scare the mutation process and co dissolve the slave's the slave's slave's previous loyalties. 

A slave is considered an investment. The Zar muse feed and cloche his slaves, keeping chem healthy and hale enough co serve him. In exchange exchange for his efforts, he expects his slaves co fight. Rival tribes will pit their slaves against each ocher in fighting rings. Since they harvest slaves from from the same places, it is all coo common co have former comrades fight each ocher in bloody death matches. Those who win these contests are accorded more freedoms and greater status, and chose with continued success can ch row off the shackles of slavery co become a full member of the tribe, possibly even displacing the Zar himself. 

The Kurgan venerate the Ruinous Powers. They see these Gods as aspects of the natural world. A stroke of lightning might be the will ofT char, the Changer of Ways, whilst an outbreak of sickness is the blessing of Nieglen, Father of Plagues. Every scone, every plant, and the very clouds chat float through che skies hold che secrets of che Gods. 

###### **SHAMANS** 

No one Ruinous Power holds more sway than the rest. An individual tribe may uphold a single God or even a pair of chem. Some tribes venerate all four and throw in a few ocher Gods as well. Generally speaking, the Kurgan know the Ruinous Powers by the names ofKhorne, Loesh (Slaanesh), Nieglin (Nurgle), and Tchar (Tzeencch). 

As the Gods are very active in the lives of the Kurgan people, their servants have incredible influence on the tribe. The shamans attach themselves co warlords who have had great success in battle, in a sense wedding themselves co a Zar. To gain the service of one of these Sorcerers is a sign of great favour by the Gods. Shamans conduce rituals, cast spells, and use foul sorcery co aid the warband in its forays against the hated Empire. Kurgan tribes dedicated co the Skull King have little use for magic, and, therefore, slay these Sorcerers wherever they are found. 

###### **KURGAN AND WAR** 

For the Kurgan, it is their duty co wage war, for war brings about the greatest change of chem all: Death. Such forays are opportunities for plunder, co advance one's position within his tribe, or even co gain the favour of the Dark Gods. Further west, the Kul, Dolgans, and Hastlings regularly harass Kislev, sending raiders ch rough the high pass co savage the _stanista_ scattered in the shadows of the mountains. The rest of the tribes conduce nearly constant warfare amongst themselves, stealing each ocher's women and supplies until some ocher tribe returns the favour. Even though raiding is a large part of Kurgan life, many make forays inco the Chaos Wastes, where they hunt for flesh or prove their might co their infernal masters. 

###### **WOMEN** 

Women occupy a strange place in the Kurgan tribe. As a people, there is no concept of marriage, only of breeding. A woman selects her maces based on his fame and prominence on the battlefield. Women who birch sons of great warriors are accorded a special place in the tribe, whilst chose who content themselves with the weak and the unsuccessful warriors are shunned until their sons prove themselves. 

Though the men provide much of the food, the women also harvest food from the steppes. Each day is spent gathering grains co grind inco flour and ocher foods culled from the flora as they pass through the land. Ac the end of the day, the women scatter seeds co replenish what they have taken for when they next pass through the land. 

Living a life of constant battle makes chis people especially hardy and 

dangerous. Warfare is a comerscone of their beliefs, and they _see_ death in battle as the ulcimace expression of divine glory. When the armies of Chaos gather in the north, the tribes of the Kurgan respond. They abandon their herding grounds co cake up arms alongside the swollen hordes of Daemons and Mutants in their crusade co wipe out the Old World. This willingness not only seems from their sense of duty co the Dark Gods but also because such wars are advantageous. The destruction of an enemy city gives the Kurgan access co more resources and keeps their own population in check. And when the war winds down, the Kurgan are just as quick co break off off from the horde co settle in their newfound land.

###### **T HE TRUTH** 

On the other side of the world, there are other Humans who serve the Dark Gods. Separated from the Kurgan by the Great Desert, they are often contained co the lands north of Cathay or across the land bridge in the northern reaches of the New Wo rld. Like the Kurgan of the Eastern Steppe, the Hung raid their neighbours, mounting attacks against the fabulous cities of Cathay or the sinister cities of the Dark Elves. They are almost constantly in a state of war. The reason is simple. They believe the purpose of their existence is to fight, co kill, co slaughter. By fighting amongst themselves, the Kurgan, and ochers, they glorify themselves and their Gods. 

Like the Kurgan, the Hung are nomads, but instead of riding horses, they use cough ponies bred for endurance and survival in the harsh climes of their hunting grounds. These people live in the saddle. Some say they are even born there. Each member of the tribe carries on his scout steed a filchy woollen tent and everything he needs to gee by. The H ung see all members of their tribe as equals and make no distinction between men and women. There are many smaller tribes including the Yin, Chi-An, Tu-Ka, Mung, Aghols, Wei-Tu, Man-Chu, Dreaded Wo, and the Kuj, though they are all part of the H ung. 

Though they owe their allegiance to the greater tribe, the H ung honour no promises and abide by no paces. They are famous for their treachery and for their will ingness to kill each o cher as well as ochers they meet. They are a sly people, cunning in their dealings and quick co double-deal. For example, they might encircle a town and promise co leave the cown unscathed if the people give over their daughters. Once the town complies wi th their wishes, the H ung butcher the cownspeople and burn down all the buildings simply because they can.
