###### **_- L IBER C HAOI'ICA_** 

Khaine is the embodiment of violence, cruelty, blood, and murder. Having long abandoned all ocher Elven Gods, the Dark Elves are a society built around the celebration of his murderous nature. But Khaine is not exclusive co these bloodthirsty Elves. No, he has a presence even amongst Humanity. Imperials associate Khaine with Morr, citing myths that link the two as brothers, each battling for control over the province of death. The Lord of Murder is upheld by killers, thieves, and even some soldiers. 

had the resolve co grasp it. Despite the efforts of the Dark Elves co eradicate it, Slaanesh's influence persiscs co this day. The reason for the cult's strength, despite constant persecution by the Witch Elves, is because of Morathi, the Witch King's mother. As she has worked co safeguard her son's place as the head of the Dark Elves, she has made unwholesome paces with the Serpent to perfect the Dark Art. 

For chose familiar with Khorne, there are coo many similarities co deny an association between the Blood God and the Lord of Murder. Those who defend Khaine claim Khorne is limited co battlefields and open war. Kho me is a Ruinous Power, a being of Chaos rather than being one of Humanity's many petty Gods. But the effect ofWidowmaker on the Elves, co say nothing of the profane practices ofKhaine's most devoted servancs, the Witch Elves, are all clear indicators of some association. 

The recent strain of a continued war effort against Ulchuan has driven Morathi into deeper wickedness. She believes ancient artefaccs lay hidden within Lustria and that to crush the High Elves for the last time, she must recover these relics. Morathi gathered a coterie of Sorceresses for a mission co the Chaos Wastes. Mounted on Dark Pegasi, they flew across the land co renew their ties co Slaanesh and take control over the Chaos tribes of the Hung. 

To the Dark Elves, there is a distinction. They deny, even unco themselves, that they serve the Blood God. They suggest Khaine is no different in scope and power &om chose same deities embraced in the Old World. The Dark Elves believe the distinaion between Khorne and Khaine is one of degree. Where Khaine is the controlled violence of ritual and religious practice, Khorne is the uncontrolled savagery of the rabid dog, the wild killing sprees undertaken by the Norsemen and ocher madmen of the Chaos Wastes. And just as the Empire takes steps co eliminate followers of Khorne, so coo do the Dark Elves snuff the lives of chose who embrace the Blood God of Chaos. 

When they arrived, they found the Hung waiting, weapons bared but unwilling co confront the beautiful women because of the raw power that emanated from chem. Even the Warlords, who rose from their council 

co face the intruders, were halted by the cries of their own Sorcerers who knew Morathi had the favour of the Pleasure Prince, Slaanesh, whom they knew as Shaarnor. Morathi, after a spectacular orgiastic ritual, summoned sixty troupes of six Daemonettes and sent chem co wipe out the Hung's rivals: the Kurgan. The Daemonettes crossed the distance and tore apart the Kurgan, sending chem Aeeing to the west, and the Hung swore oaths of allegiance co the Sorceress, thus putting an end co their raiding of the Dark Elf lands. 

Khaine's principal servancs are the Witch Elves, called the Brides of Khaine. _As_ maiden-Elves, his servants are wedded co him in midnight rites of blood sacrifice and cruel abasement. When the temple fires grow hot and the night black and cold, Khaine takes his new brides, and blood flows in torrents down the steps of his altar. 

Morathi returned to Naggaroth at the head of her new army, intending to lead chem into the foetid jungles of Lustria in search of the treasures of the Old Ones. She explained her plan co the Witch King, claiming that she would recover wonders and weapons that could surely be turned against the High Elves. Her success or failure in this effort has yet to be recorded, and the implications of the spread of Chaos remain co be seen.

###### **CHAOS CHAMPION CAREERS** 

###### **Chaos Knight** 

Chaos Knighcs are those Chaos Warriors who have served their master exceptionally well and gained a Reward for their efforts. Mose Chaos Knights are wanderers still, following a more powerful Chaos Champion. They bide their time until such point that they can prove their worth and replace him. In exchange for their improved position, Chaos Knighcs begin co forget small details of their past. They may recall important events but rarely particular details about people or places unless somehow significant co the memory. 

The career path of the Chaos Champion is long and arduous. Once a Character stares on the road of corruption, there is no turning back. He is forever bound co his fate, and there is no escaping the doom of his destiny. 

Unlike other careers in _WFRP,_ the Chaos Champion must gain a certain number of rewards prior to advancing in the esteem of his God. Rewards are granted after the Champion performs some courageous deed or overcomes his enemies. As he does so, he attraccs the Eye of his God, and when the mad orb settles on the mortal, great rewards or equal punishment may be the res ul t. For the great rewards, the risk is worth it. See page 167 for information on the Rewards of Chaos. 

To become a Chaos Knight, a Character must have gained at least one Reward of Chaos.

###### _T rappings:_ Grimoire 

_Career Entries:_ Maledictor 



**Oiapter XIII: Slaves to Chaos** 



###### **<u>r</u> Soulflaye** 

The horrid SoulAayers barely resemble their former selves, as they are riddled with mutations. These individuals are warped by the magic they wield, becoming both more and less than what they were. Mighty spell casters, SoulAayers are among the most potent servancs of Chaos, eclipsed only by the Cataclyscs. Most SoulAayers may command a coven of Malediccors, instructing chem in the arcs of Dark Magic. 



###### **<u>s</u> uraclyst** 

The Cataclyscs rival the Exalted Champions of Chaos in sheer magnitude. They can conjure up the most profane Daemons and level legions with their corrupt energy, becoming living vessels of the raw energy of Chaos. Their minds are blasted by the experiences they have endured, and they are mere shadows of their former selves. Cataclyscs always employ Daemons co do their bidding and are valued members of any Chaos Horde. 

To become a SoulAayer, you must have at least two Rewards of Chaos.

###### **GAINING R.Ew ARDS** 

The Dark Gods grant rewards only for deeds in keeping with their aims and interescs. Further, they only grant rewards when they actually notice their Champion's actions. The Dark Gods are famously disinterested in individual actions, only deigning co notice when a mortal achieves something of consequence in their profane names. 

The method of gaining Chaos Rewards and Gifts is amorphous and unpredictable. A Champion ofKhorne might slaughter 100 men and yet receive nothing from the Blood God. Another Champion might butcher a few commoners and be granted a fabulous and life-altering blessing. In essence, a GM should grant Rewards in much the same way as he would grant experience points. Each time, as the GM deems appropriate, a character receives one roll on **Table 13-1: Rewards of Chaos.** 

The easiest way co hand out Rewards is co simply grant one for every four co six sessions played. This method suggests that the mere existence of a Chaos Champion furthers the interescs of the Dark Gods, and that, undoubtedly, the Character does something co advance the cause of his

This encourages Players co co take risks and and actively work for the Gods to gain the coveted boons. 

Alternatively, you could grant them after dramatic momencs in a campaign. When a Character achieves something clearly in keeping with the interests of his Dark God, you should reward that Character appropriately. If you go with this method, you wait for the great momencs in the campaign, when something significant occurs to warrant the boon. Players will then work harder to impress their masters. The triggering event must be clearly important co the Ruinous Power the Character serves. Khorne would expect nothing less than the slaughter of hundreds, while Tzeentch might reward his minion when a particularly convoluted plan comes to fruition. Slaanesh wants followers and excess, whilst Nurgle respects those who spread his love and affiiction. You get the idea. 

Another method is to plan beforehand what the Characters need co achieve to gain the attention of their Gods. You might work a specific event inco an adventure, and if the Character does the appropriate thing, the Dark God grancs the boon. Again, such actions should be co the benefit of Chaos and carry some risk co the Champion. 

Finally, perhaps the most in keeping with the nature of Chaos is co determine randomly when a Character gains a Reward. Each month, the Player may roll ld 10. If the number matches the Dark God's favoured number (8 for Khorne, 7 for Nurgle, 6 for Slaanesh, and 9 for Tzeentch), they receive a Reward. However, what you don't tell the Player is that if they roll the number of their Dark God's enemy (Khorne opposes Slaanesh, Nurgle opposes Tzeentch), they gain a mutation instead! 

###### REw ARDS AND INSANITY 

Each time a Character gains a Chaos Reward, he gains a number of Insanity Poincs equal co 1 dl 0/5 + 1 for each point of his Magic Characteristic. He may make a special Will Power Test co reduce the 





number of Insanity Points gained. For each degree of success, he reduces the number of Insanity Poincs by 1. 

_Azgahl the Butcher gains a Chaos Reward. He rolls 1 di O and divides the result by 5. He gets a 6, so he gains 2 Insanity Points. As he does not have a Magic Characteristic, he adds nothing to his Insanity Points gained. He must now make a WiLL Power Test. His WiLL Power Characteristic is 38%, and he rolls a 27%, getting one degree of success. He reduces his Insanity Points gained by 1, giving him just 1 Insanity Point_ 

###### REw ARDS DESCRIPTIONS 

It is entirely possible, even expected, that a Champion will gain the same reward twice. Each reward includes information and guidelines for each repetitive gain. In all cases, use common sense when determining the exact effects of duplicate rewards. 

###### **~~Exalted Daemon~~** 

Your patron God finds you worthy of housing a Greater Daemon. Your _soul_ is blasted away into fragments that will drift for eternity in the Realm of Chaos. Your body, however, undergoes a shocking transformation as the Daemonic essences takes control. 

Possession is among the various calamities that can befall a mortal in the Old World. As described in **Chapter** II: **The Lost and the Damned,** some mortals willingly embrace possession, seeing it as a doorway co incredible power. Indeed, those mortals found worthy co host such a monster find their capabilities much improved, but at a terrible price. The possessing Daemon devours the soul, feeding off the life energy co sustain its presence in the mortal world. Over time, the being that once existed is annihilated, leaving only the Aesh for the Daemon co use and exploit as it wishes. 

Most cases of possession involve a Lesser Daemon, and these creatures remain just long enough co destroy the spirit of the host before retreating back co the Realm of Chaos. But when possession occurs by a Greater Daemon, the effeccs are always devastating co the mortal spirit, annihilating it utterly. 

###### **Becoming an Exalted Daemon** 

Though the mortal's identity is effectively destroyed upon becoming an Exalted Daemon, the possessing fiend must take time to develop its abilities. As a result, the Exalted Daemon functions as a career. Any Charaaer who gains Exalted Daemon as a reward must immediately abandon his current career and enter this one. It's expected that such transformations are beyond the scope of _WFRP_ games, but with the GMs permission, a Player may continue playing their Character-though we heartily advise against this. 

They change physically, resembling the Daemon that possesses them. Exalted Daemons of Khorne gain red skin, whilst those of Slaanesh might be sensual and warped. The GM is encouraged co be as descriptive as possible when devising the changed form.

###### **The of God eye**

###### **DAEMON PRINCES** 

Becoming a Daemon Prince is the greatest reward a Champion of Chaos can hope co attain. Achieved only by surviving the scrutiny of the Eye of God, only a scant few mortals are ever lifted from their world co sample the delights of Chaos at the table of their masters. Upon attaining chis distinction, the Character undergoes an awful transformation: his flesh tears from his new Daemonic form, like a new butterfly from its cocoon. Once freed, the newborn Daemon Prince is compelled co travel co the Realm of Chaos, where he will serve until found worthy enough co return to the mortal world, often more than a thousand years lacer. 

Therefore, playing newly transformed Daemon Princes are almost impossible since the Character is essentially whisked away. In some unusual instances, though, a newly created Daemon Prince is allowed to remain in the mortal world, especially in the middle of a Chaos Incursion or some ocher extenuating circumstances as determined by the GM. One interesting campaign idea is for the Player Characters to each be members of a Chaos Champion's retinue. The Chaos Champion may be a PC or simply an NPC that serves as a plot device to keep the campaign moving forward. Such games may create tensions around the gaming table in that some Characters may seem tO be unfairly rewarded. 

But, mature and experienced gamers know this is the way of Chaos. To help reduce the frustrations, have the Players take turns running the Chaos Champion tO allow each member of the group a chance to savour true power.

A exposure ny mundane co Warpscone, terrible rituals, object can acquire the characteristics or being in of the Chaos. Through presence of _Dhar,_ an ordinary thing can become far less ordinary. Witch Hunters crack suspicious materials and consign chem co the purifying fires with the merest suggestion of taint. Such things can be destroyed, often with ease. Bue every great once in a while, something from beyond chis world finds its way inco the hands of mo reals. 

This chapter presencs a different kind of Chaos Object from chose 

discussed in **Chapter V: Objects of Chaos.** These items unlikely co ever appear in the lands of honest men, only surfacing when some fool chinks he's uncovered a great prize from the bacclefield and then brings the item home co show off co his friends. Some Warlocks and their ilk may venture north co recover an item, whilst adventurers are famous for digging up some previously thought lose relic chat would have been better off co remain buried. Ultimately though, these are the cools of the Masters of Chaos, chose mortals who walk the road of damnation. 

Following the Blasphemous Objects, chis chapter also includes rules for Chaos and Daemon Weapons and Chaos Armour. These lase categories are separated as they are items granted exclusively co Champions of Chaos. 

Everything described here is wholly unsafe for the ordinary mortal. Merely handling these objeccs inspires madness and mutation. The very existence of these things defies the natural order of the universe, if such a thing exiscs at all in the world of _Warhammer._ Contained in each item's description is a new entry called Side-Effeccs. This entry details any additional effeccs the item has on ics wielder and what conditions the Character muse meet co overcome the side-effect. Use these items with caution, as they can easily create imbalances and difficulties in a campaign if handed out without regard for the consequences. 

Whilst the items are all unsafe and dangerous co the user, they can all serve as plot seeds for developing new adventures. The Characters might be hired by a suspicious merchant co recover the Beguiling Gem, or the PCs might uncover the Black Maul when exploring the comb of a Chaos Warrior. Likewise, these objeccs could be used as the climax co the adventure. A long-standing villain who has thwarted their efforcs might have been corrupted by anything presented in chis chapter. Or, the Characters could work co locate a Daemon Weapon chat has somehow fallen into the wrong hands. Evading capture, the weapon changes owners and leaves behind a trail of destruction wherever it surfaces. In shore, these objeccs are excellent devices for building campaigns chat feature Chaos.

- **History:** One of the greatest Champions of the Beastmen ever co walk the Old World was a vicious brute named Khorgor. A vile thing, it's said he butchered hundreds of Humans. So wanton was he in his killing, he decorated his horns with the entrails of the dead. Whilst a great warrior in his own right, he was aided by a pair of blasphemous axes that could hew through armour and Aesh with ease. So powerful was he when armed with these axes, no ocher Beastman could stand against him. But as with all things, Khorgor passed from this world and ownership of these terrible weapons changed hands many times, moving from successor co successor. 

###### **Beguiling Ge** **~~m~~** 

This large gemstone, seemingly an amethyst, sits in a gilt frame of platinum and sparkles in the light. Carved in ics setting are images of Daemonic women seducing mortal men. When held in the hand, worn about the neck, or pinned co the wearer's garb, this gemscone pulses with a pinkish hue. 

###### **Academic Knowledge:** Daemonology 

- **Powers:** Any Character attempting to attack the owner of the Beguiling Gem must succeed on a Challenging (-10%) Will Power Test or be unable co attack that round. The opponent may attempt a new test each round. In addition, the owner gains a +20% bonus co all Fellowship Tescs. 

- **Side-Effects:** Any Character who grasps the Beguiling Gem and who does not bear the Mark of Slaanesh must immediately succeed on a Challenging (-10%) Will Power Test or gain ldl0 Insanity Poincs as grotesque images of carnal aces and perversions course through the mind. Each time the Beguiling Gem is touched, a new Will Power Test must be made and at the same difficulty. 

- **History:** It's believed the Beguiling Gem is not a gemscone at all, but rather it is the only tear Slaanesh ever shed, crystallised by the Dark God's madness. The Beguiling Gem has changed hands many times, though the most notable occasion was when it came inco the possession of Lady Alexa Rudenhoff ofNuln. For the brief time she wore it, she was said co be the most splendid creature in all the city, and also the maddest. Two weeks was all the time that she held it. She was founded naked out front of a disreputable tavern in the Shantytown. The Watchmen reported her cause of death unknown, but the few reporcs there were claim she was covered in hundreds of terrible bite marks. 

###### **Bindings of Slaanes** **~~h~~** 

This set of dark chains and black leather scraps fitted with hooks and sharp blades is every bit as sinister as it looks. To use it, the wearer must fit the loops over his body as ifhe were wearing a harness. As soon as they are properly placed, the chains and scraps tighten, burrowing painfully inco the Aesh. The hooks and razors ensure that the wounds remain open for all co see. 

###### **Academic Knowledge:** Daemonology 

- **Powers:** When donned, the wearer aucomatically gains 1 Insanity Point. Whenever the wielder deals damage that results in a loss of a Wound, or when he himselfloses a Wound, his Strength, Toughness, and Fellowship each increase by+ ld 10% for 1 hour. In combat, the straps lash out and snare adjacent opponencs. Any creature adjacent co the wearer may not withdraw until the wearer withdraws or dies as the straps hold chem firmly in place. 

- **Side-Effects:** If worn by a creature that does not have the Mark of Slaanesh, the Bindings of Slaanesh confer no benefit. Instead, the process of tightening never stops. Each week after the first, the victim loses 2 Wounds, regardless of armour or Toughness. When the wearer is reduced co 0 Wounds, the scraps tighten completely cutting the wearer inco five separate pieces, obviously killing him in the process. Once installed, the scraps can never be removed. 

- **History:** The Bindings of Slaanesh were first encountered in the Great War Against Chaos. Though the first encounter dates some 200 years ago, the reports were very detailed. ###### **CHAOS WEAPONS** 

Chaos Weapons are greater than ordinary magic items but much less potent than the Daemon Weapons reserved for the greatest of Champions. The Chaos Weapon's properties are generated randomly. A Chaos Weapon is almost always a Hand Weapon (Sword), but there's no reason it couldn't be an axe, mace, or hammer. Some (10%) are Great Weapons. The Dark Gods disdain cowardly weapons like bows and so never reward their Champions with chem. All Chaos Weapons assume blades are used. If you prefer an axe or some ocher Hand Weapon, modify the description appropriately. 

###### **WEAPON PR.OPERTIE.5** 

A Chaos Weapon's ability is called a property. Followers of Chaos can be affected by the Weapon's properties almost as much as they can be affected by mutations, Gifcs, and Rewards. The effeccs of the property generally remain active as long as the wielder holds the weapon. 

###### **Common Propertie** **~~s~~** 

All Chaos Weapons have certain qualities in common, regardless of their individual properties. 

- Every Chaos Weapon has a magical aura. Characters with the Magical Sense Skill aucomatically sense this aura as a swirling cloud of black mist. 

- Chaos Weapons can damage creatures listed as being immune to the effects of normal weapons. 

- Owning a Chaos Weapon makes it harder co resist mutations . Characters take a -10% penalty co all cescs made co resist gaining new mutations. 

###### **DETERMINING PROPER TIE.5** 

A Chaos Weapon may have any number of properties, but it cannot have the same property more than once. Any duplicates must be rerolled until a new property is determined. Each time a Chaos Weapon is granted as a Reward, the Weapon gains a new property. If the weapon is bescowed co a Champion of a particular Chaos God, roll on one of **Tables 14- 4** through **14- 7,** depending on the Dark God the Character serves. 

###### **~~Animated~~** 

The blade shakes and jumps in its scabbard or hanger. When used in combat, it settles down and performs as a normal sword. At your mental command (a half action), the blade _Ries_ from your hand co continue the fight against your foe. It continues co fight in the air so long as you remain within 6 yards (3 squares) of it. You do not gain any of the weapon's capabilities when yo u wield it. When fighting independently, it uses the following profile.

Since Player Characters should almost never gain these weapons, a GM has some latitude in their design.

#### **IMI.NN>** 

High Elves, and even the Runemagic of the Dwarfs certainly don't follow the teachings of the Orders of Magic, but, they are not Dark Magic either. In this sense, Dark Magic implies the reckless use of magic employed by Witches and Warlocks, those individuals who are self-taught in their arrs.

It also encompasses that which is employed by the Necromancers, the process of using the Winds of Magic to create and control the spirirs of the dead. ###### **USING DARK MAGIC**

dangerous qualities of the agents of Chaos. Frequent use of Dark Magic not only damages reality, but it also presents an incredible risk co the caster himself, resulting in a myriad of unexpected side-effects, not co mention the increased risk of triggering Tzeentch's Curse. 

protestations to the contrary. The loosed strands of energy do not dissipate on their own; once conjured and rendered into their twisted form, they remain, changing the environment in subcle ways at first, until the corruption becomes so great that it warps the very landscape, as has happened in the Chaos Wastes and in pockets throughout the Old World. Some believe this extra energy can be harnessed, used co fuel terrible spells and forge blasphemous items of Chaos. Ochers claim this stuff eventually coalesces co become Warpscone. Ochers still say it is what some Magisters see with their witch sight, the manifestations of magic gone awry. No one knows for certain what happens to this energy except co note casting spells in areas rich with _True Dhar,_ as some call it, have spectacular effects. 

Risks aside, the true appeal of using Dark Magic is the power it offers. Instead of being confined to a single Wind, the caster can use as many or as few winds as there are available at the time of the casting. This always results in loosing strands of unchecked energy that manifescs itself in strange ways, for the spell icself (or the ritual for that matter) is magic in its most raw, unruly form. It is because of this that the Colleges of Magic and the Witch Hunters are so keen co track down and execute users of Dark Magic-and not for some ethical reason, despite 

###### **W11CKE1tt** 

itchsight _(i.e._ the Magical Sense Skill) is the ability of most W spellcasters co sense the presence or absence of Magic. All people born with the talent co work magic have some degree of witchsight that can be developed and expanded with training so the spellcaster can actually see the ebb and Aow of the Winds of Magic, witness the scintillating colours of the Chaos energy in its raw form, and be better able co harness it for the casting of spells. For more information on the development and function of witchsight, be sure to reference _Realms of Sorcery_ page 46. 

###### **CHAOS MADE FI.ESH** 

Having the ability co sense magic enables Magisters and their ilk co better control the energies they wield. Aside from ics utility, witchsight also reveals an abundance of odd manifestations, eerie phenomena, and sometimes glimpses of the future and the past. Most Magisters learn co cope with the sometimes unsettling visions they experience, reminding themselves chat their art is one of mysteries that are impossible to unravel. But some phantasms are coo frightening, coo maddening to ignore. These are the vestiges, the essence of Chaos formed into something that resembles Aesh, but is intangible, insubstantial, and can affect the world in no significant way-or so the Magisters say. 

The things of the Aethyr, for lack of a better term, are harbingers, apparitions foretelling some significant event. They may take the form of a nest of wriggling maggocs, the fiery forms of long-dead witches, or even 





<!-- Start of picture text -->
20'/<br><!-- End of picture text -->

a pack of ghoscly hounds that breathe fire and shower sparks wherever they step. Despite their macabre and disgusting appearance, they seem to have no power over those who see them. 

So, what then, are these things that only those with witchsight can see? There are many theories, ranging from Daemons struggling to breach the barrier between the world of men and the Realm of Chaos co hallucinations brought on as a result of dabbling in the forbidden. What is known for certain is the apparitions always appear in the aftermath of some significant magical event, as if they were drawn to the instance, somehow compelled to witness the caster in his act of magic use. More importancly, the same harbingers tend to appear time and again when certain conditions are met. For instance, the Handmaidens (see _WFRP_ page 211) always manifest themselves after excessive use of Gold or Celestial Magic. The Rotwyrms seem drawn co Jade and Amethyst Magic, and so on. Since these apparitions appear again and again, there must be some reason for their appearance, and they muse fulfil some purpose. 

###### **THE TRUTH** 

The apparitions are as real as Daemons and as real as the Dark Gods themselves. Their existence is a window inco the very nature of Chaos. Without the existence of Mankind, Chaos would have little power, since Chaos and its minions are reflections of the psyches and nightmares of mortals. Feeding on fear and misgiving, Chaos takes shape, becoming on fear and misgiving, Chaos takes shape, becoming fear and misgiving, Chaos takes shape, becoming

###### **USING APPARITIONS** 

Apparitions may serve a variety of purposes in a _WFRP_ game. They may be nothing more than sim ple warnings co Players that they use magic coo recklessly. They remind the spellcaster that his doom is imminent if he continues down the path. However, they can also function in more important ways. An apparition might appear as a warning that something strange and magical has recently occurred. It might reveal the presence of Daemonic activity, or offer a clue about some sinister plot. A character that uses Magical Sense when walking inco a room that once held a possessed mortal might see reflections of the Daemon in a mirror. Or, if a Character uses witchsight in an area of particularly strong emotion, such as a murder scene, he might catch glimpse of blood running fro m the walls. ###### **SEASONS AND SKIES**

ne of the central strengths of the Chaos Sorcerer is the ability tO Oconjure Daemons from the Realm of Chaos. They can call upon the infernal legions tO do their bidding (most of the time). Up until now, _summoning Daemons_ fell under the Lore of Chaos Spell (though there are rituals enabling more permanent effecrs). ###### **DAEMONIC FAMILIARS** 

Sorcerers can use Daemon Summoning Rituals to gain Daemonic Familiars. As with Wizards who bind or create Familiars (see _Realms of Sorcery_ page 183), Sorcerers can benefit from the service of a Daemonic helper, an assistant that lends its power and expertise to the spellcaster. Like other Familiars, Daemons can improve a Wizard's power, giving him or a boost to his magical strength even storing magical energy. Though the rewards are great, they are not without risk. 

###### **CALLING** THE **FAMILIAR** 

To call a Daemonic Familiar, you must have access to a ritual that summons Least Daemons. (Theoretically, it may be possible to use a more powerful

Daemon as a Familiar, but these beings are better able co resist the magic chat would bind chem.) You muse also have a Magic Characteristic of2 and the Academic Knowledge (Daemonic) and Speak Arcane Language (Daemonology) Skills. Though not required, a occogram is a useful cool co help keep the Lease Daemon throughout the bargaining process. 

###### **BARGAINING FOR SER VICE** 

Once the ritual is complete and the Daemon appears, you muse bargain with the fiend co gain ies service. The process is simple. You muse succeed on a Hard (-20%) Fellowship Test opposed by the Daemon's Will Power Test. If you fai l, you may cry again each day for a number of days equal co your Magic Characteristic. If you do not manage co secure a bargain, the Daemon returns co the Realm of Chaos from whence it was summoned (though if a occogram is used, and if it's damaged, the Daemon may escape co do what it wishes in the mortal world). 

You can reduce the difficulty of your Fellowship Test by offering gifts and promises co the Daemon. The better the gift, the more agreeable the Daemon becomes, making the challenge of convincing it co serve you all the easier. Possible gifts and their corresponding reductions co difficulty could include: 

- _Immortal Soul:_ If the caster offers his immortal soul chat the Daemon can claim at the end of its service, reduces the difficulty by two seeps. 

- _Limited Service:_ Limiting the service co a number of years reduces the difficulty by one seep, co a number of months by two seeps, and the number of days by three seeps. 

- _Sacrifice:_ For each sentient mortal sacrificed co the Daemon, decrease the difficulty by two seeps. For every animal sacrificed co the Daemon, decrease the difficulty by one seep. 

Negotiating service can also be handled through role-playing. The GM should decide beforehand what the Daemon wanes (the eyes of children, a steady supply of blood, worship, Human sacrifice and so on) and then bargains for service based on how closely the caster comes co the Daemon's desires. So long as the terms favour the Daemon, the GM may do away with the opposed Tests and simply grant the Familiar co the Sorcerer. 

###### **DAEMONIC FAMILIAR MOTIVES** 

Daemons exist co corrupt and destroy, and so even if bound by strict terms of service, the Daemon always works against his master. He will not overdy betray him, but he will work co put his master into dangerous positions, putting his master's life at risk or simply making life more difficult. Canny Wizards include provisions in their negotiations co lessen the risk of a prolonged relationship with the Daemon. 

The Daemonic Familiar should always be run as an NPC. GMs should feel free co use these creatures as plot devices, foils, or even as antagonises for the Character chat summoned it. This said, the Familiar should not be such a risk chat the Character regrets binding the Daemon. Instead, the Character should always wonder what his Daemon intends, why it does what it does, and be on the look out for the Daemon's betrayals (minor as they may be). 

###### IMPROVING FAMILIARS 

Once the caster binds the Familiar, the Daemon automatically enters the Familiar Career (though it gains none of the listed Skills and Talenes and must buy chem as it gains experience points). This is the same career chat bound or created Familiars use. Familiars gain experience points at half the rate of their masters: _i.e.,_ for every 200 points a Familiar's master accumulates, the Familiar earns 100. Familiars never earn experience poines on their own. In addition co spending experience on advancement picks from the Familiar creature career advance

###### **PERIL: FAMILIAR DANGERS** 

Familiars, in addition co being powerful companions, can also be dangerous co their masters. The fo llowing sections describe the ways chis can manifest. 

###### **A of Sorcer Sign** **<u>y</u>** 

Daemonic Familiars are clear signs of complicity with the Ruinous Powers. Normal Familiars are often grounds enough for harassment by Witch Hunters and ocher opponents of Chaos, but having a Daemon in one's employ is grounds for immediate persecution and destruction. 

###### **~~Attention of Chaos~~** 

Daemonic Familiars are sometimes granted as Rewards-as clear a sign as any chat the Dark God has an interest in the Character's career. Those who conjure Daemonic Familiars are likely co attract even more attention, drawing to chem Daemons and ocher agents of Chaos. 

###### **~~Obsession~~** 

Because of the close relationship the master and Familiar share, it is possible for the master co become utterly obsessed with his magical servant. Every time the Familiar spends experience points on an advancement or new ability, its master must make an Easy (+20%) Fellowship Test. If he fails, he becomes obsessed with his Familiar-its activities, its whereabouts, ies choughes and opinions. In addition co roleplaying chis obsession, it gives ochers an easy (if figurative) chain co yank. Anyone threatening or otherwise using the Familiar against its master (GM's judgment) causes such psychological disturbance within the master chat he suffers a -10% penalty co his Intelligence and Will Power, and a -20% penalty co his Fellowship, until the situation is resolved. 

###### **Death or** **~~e~~ Depauur** 

Unlike ocher Magiscers and their Familiars, Chaos Sorcerers have no emotional ties co their thralls. The Dark Wizard never cakes a penalty once his minion is released or slain. However, Daemons are spiteful creatures and almost always seek revenge on their former masters. For one week after the Familiar is released or dies, anytime the Sorcerer triggers Tzeentch's Curse on a Casting Roll, the severity of the curse worsens by one seep co a maximum of Catastrophic Failure. The Daemon's revenge lases for one week before it loses interest and picks on someone or something else. 

###### **Aethyric Ijnk** 

Familiars have a special link co their masters, and, because of chis link, enemy spellcascers can exploit the bond. _As_ such, spellcasters can use another Wizard's Familiar as a special ingredient co augment spells 

targeting the Familiar's master. The Familiar adds a+ 1 bonus to the Casting Roll. When used in chis way, the Familiar experiences intense pain and must succeed on a Challenging (-10%) **Z.~~...** Will Power Test or cake a Damage 1 hit. If it cakes a critical with a value of 5 or more, it explodes messily. Naturally, sane Familiars do what they can co avoid being used in chis way. 

A Wizard cannot use his own Familiar co gee a bonus when he cases spells co affect himself. A Wiz.ard's allies could conceivably use a Familiar to cast friendly spells on ies master, but a Wizard who frequently allowed chis would face open rebellion from his Familiar in very short order.

Ipitting legions n the Realm of of Chaos, the Dark Gods unruly forms against one another in a game wage war against each ocher, of perpetual conflict. ###### **TYPES OF DAEMONS** 

Though they are birched of Chaos, there seems a strange order co the Daemon spawn of the Dark Gods. Scholars have identified types of Daemon, ranked by relative levels of power, and councless in number. Each seems unique in their awfulness, but they are also alike. There are distinct forms chat arise co curse the Old World time and again, each foul type fulfilling a particular role in some unknowable master plan. Merciless predacors, it's believed they know the scent of every mortal creature. They are relentless crackers, crossing seas and mountains co reach their prey. ###### **NURGLINGS** 

Nurglings are the very image of Father Nurgle himself, having friendly, mischievous faces and bloated, green bodies fitted with disproportionate limbs. The only difference is their size. A Nurgling is no caller than a foot high. These foul things inhabit the bodies of larger Daemons, preferably the Great Unclean Ones who spawn chem. Nurglings creep into the crevices, burying themselves beneath the diseased flab of their bulky forms and suckle on the cancerous wounds chat weep foul pus. While covering their hose, they jockey for the favour of their master, purring with pleasure when caressed or squealing with delight when offered a choice morsel of flesh. 

Such Nurglings may look for ochers of their kind-they are indeed sociable creatures, but many content themselves in the filch and squalor of Human cities, feasting on offal piles, sewers, and the like. Bue from time co time, the Nurgling will seek out its Human hose out of some strange affection, co visit a plague as a means of gratitude. 

Even as disgusting as they are, nothing compares co how they are often created. A Nurgling grows in the rotting flesh of a Great Unclean One. Like infancs, they feed on the nucriencs of the mother, though in chis case, it is the rancid milk of pestilence. In time, a diet of filch enables the Nurgling co grow large enough co allow it co eat ics way out of the wee innards, born co whatever horrid existence it faces. Queerly, Great Unclean Ones tend co see these vermin as their children. They coddle chem, coo at chem, and caress chem, showering chem with affeccionchough such endearmencs are no obstacle co the Greater Daemon's tantrums and boccomless hunger. Many Nurglings roe away, gee caught between the Daemon's prodigious coes, or are dissolved in ics gastric juices. 

Nurglings rarely attack a foe by themselves, preferring instead co gather in swarms of chattering, gibbering green bodies. They claw and bite at their foe's legs, biting ankles and licking at any interesting sores or abrasions they discover. They have tiny teeth as sharp as razors and leave festering little bites on their victims but rarely kill chem outright.

###### **BEASTS OF NURGLE** 

###### _The Beasts, Slime Hounds_ 

The horrid Beascs ofNurgle are massive lumbering fiends that are as stupid as they are ugly-and they are hideously ugly. The product of coo much corruption in an area, these things combine the features or several different creatures, creating a terrifying abomination. The Beast's body is that of a massive, black-spotted slug that glistens with dewy excretions and is copped by a massive head with a large, drooling, fang-filled mouth ringed in tentacles that drip a paralytic coxin. Growing all along the length of ics moist body are razor-sharp spines that stick out in random places. About midway down the trunk, a pair of useless legs ending in clawed and webbed feet flop about uselessly. The thing's body ends in a long tail fitted with a sharp stinger. Though somewhat uniform in appearance, the Beascs are heavily corrupted and sport many mutations and alterations, giving these creatures a wide array of unpredictable abilities and features. 

Beascs ofNurgle seem co serve no purpose whatsoever. They are unreliable on the battlefield, crushing their own forces as much as their enemies with their flailing. The things move very slowly, and everything dies that couches the slime trails they leave. In fact, so great is their stink that birds fall from the sky, trees wither and die, and grass for scores of feet all around turns co ash. They are excitable creatures that behave in the most unpredictable ways. 

The Beasts ofNurgle congregate in herds near the edge of the swirling darkness that marks the border between the Umbra and the Realm of Chaos, feeding on Nurglings and ocher Daemons that spill out from the Aethyr. Rare! y, these herds slip south, into the hunting territory of the Kurgan and Hung where many of these creatures wind up as food for the cook pots. Beasts ofNurgle are only seen during Incursions, but liars and madmen have claimed co see chem, spinning wild scories about how friendly these things are.

###### **PLAGUEBEARERS** 

###### _Plaguebearers, Tainted Ones, Maggorkin, Rotbearers, Talrymen of Plagues_ 

The Plaguebearers are the vile Lesser Daemons ofNurgle. Charged with counting all the poxes and contagions in the world, they breach the boundaries between the mortal world and the Realm of Chaos co spread woe and despair, spilling their filch wherever they go. And in their deep bass voices, they mutter and grumble, naming and counting the diseases that affiict mankind. 

The Maggockin are especially foul, humanoid in shape but savaged by sickness and hunger. At the centre of their being is a grossly distended abdomen, split in places co reveal the gushing organs within and the wriggling maggots that feast on the roe. Resting above this prodigious bulk is a gaunt rib cage covered by thin green or ochre flesh that estifies co co their master's nature. Two spindly limbs just barely bear 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
estifies co co  their master's nature. Two spindly limbs just barely bear<br><!-- End of picture text -->



their sack-like bodies, bent by pestilence so virulent it warps the bones. Of all of their features, it is the egg-shaped head perched on a thin neck that's the most disturbing. Its single, large eye situated in the centre of its face weeps thick sludge, shadowed by the horn that pierces the cankerous flesh on ics brow. Beneath the eye is a wormy mouth, slick with the filch dripping from is ro lling eye. It is a thing co be detested, but it is a thing of power. 

Venerated by the Chaos cul cs of the Lord of Despair, the Tai need Ones are living symbols ofNurgle's blessings, personifying all that the Dark God is. By embracing the nature of these fiends, the cultists learn co accept their own corruptions and grow beyond chem. Those few who foolishly stand against the Plaguebearers, they learn a terrible lesson about slow, leprous death.

###### **<u>s</u> Using Plaguebearer** 

Followers of Nurgle are often indistinguishable from the trains of plague victims forced co wander from town co town, driven on by their countrymen's unwill ingness to aid chem. Those processions that venerate the Lord of Decay are often granted Plaguebearers co guide chem on their travels, shepherding chem along like so many leperous sheep. ###### **FIENDS OF SLAANESH** 

The Fiends of Slaanesh prowl the Chaos Wastes in packs, attacking groups of Kurgan, Hung, and Dark Elves. On occasion, a group of Fiends may descend into Norsca or elsewhere, destroying livestock and abducting townsfolk. Their attacks may seem at first the work of animals, but a Follow Trail Test indicates something far more sinister. 

_Beasts of Slaanesh, Bestials, Rams of Slaanesh, U nho{y Ones_ 

The Hunting Beasts of Slaanesh are a foul race of Daemonic creatures. Spawned from the mad mind of the Serpent, these creatures combine several traits of scorpion, Human and reptile to become some unholy abomination. The main body of the Fiend is white or some other pastel hue and segmented, ending in a broad stinger tail that drips with venom. Four roughly humanoid legs branch out from the rear body to give the creature stability. From the front of the lithe body grows a Humanoid torso covered in a row of breasts and a pair of arms. The Fiend's head is reptilian, not too unlike that of a monitor lizard, but with a longer prehensile tongue. ItS emerald, alien eyes perch on either side of itS head, rolling about in itS skull. 

###### **STEEDS OF SLAANESH** 

_Flesh Lickers, Tongue Flayers, Degraded Ones, Whips of Slaanesh_ 

The Steeds of Slaanesh are strange, disturbing creatures that roam in herds along the borders of the Realm of Chaos. Gifted to Champions of Slaanesh or sometimes ridden by the alluring Daemonettes, the Steeds are excellent servants, carrying their riders across uncertain terrain with natural grace and incredible speed, while lashing out at foes with their whip-like tongues. 

Fiends are base creatures that scour the Chaos Wastes in search of victims (innocent or otherwise) to torment. Barely above the mutated predators that share the same grounds in terms of intellect, these things are vicious omnivores, taking great pleasure in sampling the flesh of their still-living victims. 

Like all creatures of Slaanesh, the Steeds have a perverse beauty, 

combining elegance and sleekness with an unnatural appearance. They are bipedal, with a body shape not unlike that of an ostrich, _sans_ feathers. It has two long, feminine legs, and a crest of vivid green hair that runs down the length of its back. The glossy fur on its legs and upper body is typically lavender, whilst the head, tail, and underside are pastel yellow with mot tled deep red markings. About halfway down itS long neck, there sometimes grows a vertical row of breasts, marking this thing as a creature of the Serpent. The most disturbing quality of this creature is its conical head equipped with a sphincter-like mouth. Flitting out from this orifice is a long, electric-blue, whip-like tail that ends in a sharp barb.

###### **DAEMONETTES** 

_Children of Slaanesh, Bringers of Joyous Degradation, Givers of Indescribable Delight, Debauched Ones, Seekers of Decadence_ 

The Daemonettes are powerful symbols of Slaanesh. Existing only to serve his twisted will, in some ways they are extensions of the Prince of Pleasure, exulting in the sensual experiences they enjoy and inflicting pain co excite their depraved sensibilities. Though they are often used as soldiers of Slaanesh in war, on occasion, the Serpent may bescow one of these creatures onco a mortal as some kind of perverse gift that almost always kills its recipient. 

Like all creatures of the Lord of Pain and Pleasure, Daemonettes are horrific and disturbing beings. No right-thinking creature should find beauty in these merciless killers, and yet these Daemons somehow transfix and beguile onlookers, bending chem co their unspeakable will. They have creamy, pale skin and large, emerald pools for eyes, but instead of hair, most have horny bone ridges. Instead of hands, their arms end in scythelike talons, much like a crab's claw. These man-sized Daemons stand upon two legs that end in two-coed feet fitted with black talons. 

Given their grotesque appearances, it's hard co imagine these beings as seducers. History has proved time and again that their entrancing presence and honeyed words have lured many a mortal co an agonising death. The Daemonette transfixes the weak-willed as a snake charms a mouse, drawing ever closer, moving surely, forming sensual words on her perfect lips, deluding, seducing, until she can plunge her talons inco her foe. As the mortal dies, his life-blood spilling out in corrents, she laughs the thrill of the kill and the ecstasy and pain of the morcal's death titillating her capricious whim.

###### **PINK HORRORS** 

Tzeentch's Lesser Daemons are known as Pink Horrors. Unique in their form's utter unpredictability, Pink Horrors are shapeless masses of solid magic that undulate and transform, cycling through a myriad of different shapes and colours, ever changing, always in a state of becoming. New faces push out against their rubbery hides only co retreat as the section is replaced by a new flap of skin or a nest of writhing tentacles. They amble along, warping everything they couch, spraying showers of multicoloured sparks with incredible bursts. 

Their behaviour is no less random. One Pink Horror might caper and gambol about, tearing at ics strange flesh, while another shrieks and giggles like the maddest of men. Some grumble and lash out, letting loose terrifying shrieks or screams of nonsense, and ochers are utterly silent, nearly immobile, trembling with barely contained energy. 

Pink Horrors congregate in packs, the magic in their forms harmonising co reach new levels of potency. A single Pink Horror is capable of loosing gouts of eldritch fire, but when gathered in herds, they can change the very fabric of realities, launching waves of changing energy that wreaks havoc with their opponencs' forms. Don't believe for a minute that simply slaying these things is the answer. Many warriors have done just this only co find themselves facing twice as many of these horrid things.

###### **TRUE NAMES**

But often the research and struggle is worth it, for these names offer a mortal leverage when dealing with the Daemon. 

Daemons do their best co keep their True Names hidden. They never reveal their names unless faced with utter annihilation, though almost all are willing co cough up the name of a weaker and less significant Daemon in exchange for freedom. Other avenues for finding True Names include grimoires and forbidden tomes. Some say that within the most

_Fists of Khorne, Drinkers of Blood, Lords of Skulls, Eaters of Gore and Flesh, Deathbringers of Khorne, Blooded Ones, Guardians of the Throne, Hig~handed Slayers_ 

The Lords of Skulls are the Greater Daemons of Khorne. They are the brightest and most powerful servantS of the Blood God. Indeed, they are the most favoured of all of Khorne's servantS. Their bloodlust extends far beyond mortal comprehension, and no amount of killing, no quantity of corpses is ever enough, for the FistS ofKhome ever wane more death. 

One may talk with a Bloodchirster, for they speak all the tongues of mortals, every dialect, every strain. This is oflictle avail, for all chat the Lords of Skulls wish is to slaughter the world and lay its steaming carcass at the feet ofKhorne. The Bloodthirscer exists only to ki ll, raising its head to the brooding sky to take in the stink of blood and death as it claims yet more skulls for the Skull Throne. 

On the battlefield, the Bloodthirster is the master of war. He binds his legions to his murderous will, driving his forces to aces of greater slaughter that exalt the name of Khorne. They are beings of incredible cunning, instinctively capable of defeating the best and brightest mortal generals. They can sense which way a battle is flowing, instantly seizing the chance to use their blades and troops to the greatest effect. 

When they join the battle, they are terrifying opponentS. With each sweep of their dreaded rune axes, they level entire regiments. Their mere presence scorches the earth with potential violence, and the beating of their wings stirs up violent storms as if awakening the very skies co the hatred chat boils in Khorne's veins. Ic is especially dangerous in that it combines malign intelligence with brute strength. No man can stand against the Bloodchirscer, for it throws itself into every fight with abandon, butchering anything it can with no regard for itSelf. Ic screams challenges to mortal foes, heedless of the consequences of itS hate. What's worse is the appearance of such a creature emboldens the ocher servants of the Blood God, inciting chem to near suicidal frenzies. As walking Demigods of death, nothing shore of an entire army can hale the progress of this implacable foe. 

###### **MANIFESTATION** 

A birch of a Bloodchirscer into the Old World ravages the land, sending waves of rippling wickedness in all directions, infecting mortals with itS hate and thirst for violence. For miles around, the sky darkens, taking on a ghastly hue as clouds, swollen with blood, race across the firmament, ill ing torrents of crimson rain onto the land. Black lightning flashes 

amidst these stinking abominations, lancing from the Chaos-wracked heavens to sec fire co the earth. 

_As_ the Greater Daemon draws closer co itS enemies, waves of itS essence roll from itS massive form, contaminating the heartS and minds of those mortals in its path. Tempers shorten, and emotions run wild. Fights break out over minor or even just perceived offences, and as the Daemon draws closer, the conflictS turn violent as former friends struggle to kill one ocher due to the rage chat burns in their hearts. Ocher phenomena testify to the Bloodthirscer's power. Animals turn rabid, acting strange and attacking without provocation. The Daemon's presence causes plane life co change, growing thorns or even teeth that gnash at the air, searching for the flesh of the living. And worse of all, inanimate objects perspire. Beads of black blood dot the surface and run, dripping down the lengths of blades or mixing with the fluid in cups.

_Slayers of Slaanesh, Feasters of Pain, Base Ones, Despoilers of the Flesh, Great Horned Ones_ 

Passion, pleasure, pain, and inspiration: these are the hallmarks of the Keeper of Secrets. The Greater Daemons of Slaanesh personify limitless experience and unfettered desire, the very concepts born into Aesh. They are repulsive and horrific, yet they transfix mortals with a monstrous allure that defies explanation. 

The Base Ones are ultimate licence. They exist to evoke the senses, to create, to experience, and to exult in the mortal whims of passion. They also dull the mind, making it harder to appreciate the ordinary and the mundane. They are the pain of failure, the agony of excess, and that which drives mortals to more daring acts to escape the ordinary. 

Like a dancer, the Greater Daemon moves with liquid grace, Aitting about like the gentle brush of a lover's fingers on the Aesh. Wherever it ll goes, a becomes possible. But when it passes, it leaves behind anguish and agony, as real and as painful as the sharp stab of a cruel knife. And all those who have known the greatest pleasure are wracked with despair and loss, uprooting themselves from the normal experience co follow after the haunted promises of the Great Horned Ones as they sway to the tune of Slaanesh's wicked laughter. 

###### **MANIFESTATIONS** 

The moment a Base One appears in the world, the tendrils of Slaanesh's foul will spreads, carried on the Winds of Magic to tantalize and torment mortals for miles around. There is an unclean trembling in all things, potential struggling for release. Mortals break out into sweaes, and their hearts pound against their cheses. Animals become inAamed and tum violent, kicking against their stalls or tearing against their harnesses. Weapons throb with invisible tumescent energy. Wood shivers and warps. The trees creak, and the earth yawns, gushing merry water from its depths. Inhibitions fade, old loyalties dim, and the bonds of trust weaken. Passion fills the heares and minds of all, and if unchecked, mortals revel in wild abandon. 

But the physical tingling of desire is not all that resules from the hint of a Keeper. Artises become feverishly inspired, fanatically sketching and drawing, creating masterpieces far beyond their skill. From the lips of poees come exquisite verse that perfectly captures sorrow absolute or unabashed desire. From the throaes of singers spill songs of such beauty that those who hear it die from broken heares. The Daemon fills the dreams of mortals with such _visions_ of beauty that they thrash about weeping for the unachievable perfection of their nightmares. When they awaken, their days are spent in melancholy, yearning for that which they cannot have and can never attain. 

They murder without thought, compassion, or remorse-killing just to see the aesthetic in the spray of blood or the pitch of a dying man's scream. Witty and capricious, they indulge in every fantasy with cruel and selfish abandon, caring not one whit for those they harm. 

###### **APPEARANCE** 

The Keeper of Secrees is awful to behold. It takes the form of an androgynous being of impossible stature. Ies four arms, two of which end in pincers, beckon and weave as it sways to the music of mortal delight and the hurt that resules from over-indulgence. Its huge jewelled eyes contain the secrees of pleasure and pain, hidden !uses and terrifying impulses. Its pastel skin exudes a narcotic musk that aces to magnify the senses, enrapture the spirit, and thrust dark impulses into the minds and heares of mortals. 

Its head, sometimes human, sometimes bestial, is ringed with a nest of curved horns that glisten with an oily sheen. A serpent's tongue writhes from between its razored teeth, tasting the air and the perverse energy contained within. A number of swollen breases cling to the left side of its torso, like vast obscene ticks. It stands upon strong legs that give way to almost reptilian claws. It strides the earth, clad in an elaborate costume of bizarre colours and exotic materials, from iron-hard chains to the softest velvets. Horrific as it is, it nevertheless commands the eye, whatever it happens to be doing. 

###### **CAP ABILITIES** 

When a Keeper of Secrets appears, all hope is lost. Ies presence wreaks havoc with the minds of those mortals around it, interfering with their ability to concentrate, distracting them with ies unnatural charisma. The Base One dances through battle, sliding past regiment and would-be hero alike, exulting with each slash of ies pincers, _its_ laughter mingling with the screams of the dying. 

On and off the battlefield, the Keeper of Secrees easily dominates mortals with its otherworldly allure. Those who fall victim to the Despoiler's glamour do anything to please their master, forgetting all that is decent as they loose themselves in the Daemon's aura. 

When this game becomes tired, dull, done, the Base One will likely plunge its pincers deep into their slave's Aesh, pausing to experience the heat of the organs throbbing their last, to drink in the fading light of their eyes, before scattering the carcass into bloody gobbees. This fate, perhaps, is better than abandonment by the Great Horned One, for once a creature has basked in ies presence, nothing will sate their overwhelmed senses ever again.

Extreme change is not a natural thing. Beneath every plot, every event, every cum of face, there lays the machinations of Lord Tzeencch. In the interests of perpetual change, Tzeencch demands the world remain in a constant state of flux, always unfolding, always al cering, crapped in a constant process of becoming. Tzeencch blessed the Lords of Change, his Greater Daemons, with the ability co see into the future and the past, co see the larger workings of the unfolding randomness chat makes up the foundations of reality. Armed with incredible cunning and the timeless wisdom of their infernal master, they detest the confining bindings chat stability and familiarity represent. ###### **MANIFESTATIONS**

From sudden and powerful storms, co random mutations chat riddle che flesh of che innocent, nothing is beyond che capabilities of these Greater Daemons. ###### **APPEARANCE** 

When a Lord of Change reveals itself, it is a vision of horror. A massive feathered creature with the head of carrion bird wobbling on cop of a warded neck, it seems almost frail, almost coo weak co support what it does. No secret can be kept from the all-seeing gaze of a Lord of Change, for all ambitions and woes are laid bare before ies immortal scare. With bright multi-coloured wings, and a gigantic bird-like face, a Lord of Change is the most bizarre of all Greater Daemons. Ics skin writhes with unnatural energies-magic courses through ies warping body as blood pumps through a mortal.

Many adventurers have underestimated these strange creatures, chinking their wiry frames and fluttering wings fragile, only for their lances and swords co shatter against ies immortal skin.
